how khosla ventures invests in deep tech , with kanu gulati and rajesh swaminathan 
 deep tech : from lab to market with benjamin joffe 
 technology 
 khosla ventures ( kv ) has been an active investor in deep tech for 15 years . in this episode they share ideas on how they select sectors to invest in and prioritize and retire risk , how to best support startups , and what investors need to enter the deep tech field ( hint : it 's not a phd ) . 
 this podcast is hosted by benjamin joffe , partner at sosv , a global early stage fund focused on deep tech . sosv runs multiple accelerator programs including hax ( intelligent hardware ) and indiebio ( life sciences ) . to hear about new episodes , sign up to the newsletter or follow us on twitter at @ lab to market . 
 overview 
 kanu gulati and rajesh swaminathan are investment partners focused on deep tech at khosla ventures . the firm was founded by vinod khosla -- co-founder of sun microsystems ( acquired by oracle for us $ 7 . 4 billion in 2009 ) and former general partner at kleiner perkins -- with the goal of ‘ reinventing social infrastructure with technology ’ , to elevate the entire planet ’s quality of life without destroying it . 
 over the past 15 years , kv has raised over $ 5 b across 6 funds and invested in about 400 startups including impossible foods , rocket lab , doordash , openai and many more . 
 they invest mostly at early stage — signing checks ranging from a few hundred $ k , up to $ 50 million — and without shying away from the high technical risk of deep tech . 
 after an introduction and examples from kv ’s portfolio , the conversation goes into : 
 why it is crucial to prioritize risks and retire them in the right order . 
 the 12 different technologies that can move the needle for the climate crisis . 
 their approach to detecting startups from centers of excellence . 
 what sectors kv focuses on , including climate tech , hyperlocal and bio - manufacturing , hardware acceleration for ai , and more . 
 what investment and operating partners do . 
 how they support their portfolio in particular with recruiting ( white paper ) . vinod khosla even calls himself a ‘ glorified recruiter ’ ! 
 how conviction , immersion , patience and staying power matter more than a phd to start investing in deep tech . 
 how more engagement between financial and corporate vcs , building more forums and reducing inefficiencies in the deep tech ecosystem could help .

 history 
 the firm was founded in 2004 by vinod khosla , a former general partner of kleiner perkins . [ 2 ] khosla ventures 's first two investment vehicles were funded with his own personal capital and were not open to institutional investors . [ 3 ] 
 khosla ventures fund iii secured $ 1 billion to invest in traditional early stage and growth stage companies . khosla also raised $ 300 million for khosla seed , which would invest in higher - risk opportunities and science experiments . [ 4 ] by 2013 , the company was considered one of the top investors in clean technology and had invested in more than 70 companies in the sector . [ 5 ] as of october 2015 [ update ] , khosla ventures was one of the five largest and most active investors in the space sector . [ 6 ] 
 in september 2017 , khosla ventures had about $ 5 billion in assets under management . [ 7 ] 
 in october 2021 , khosla ventures announced that it had raised $ 1 . 4 billion in funding to invest in early - to - late stage startups , breaking down to $ 400 million for seed deals and $ 1 billion for later - stage companies . [ 8 ] 
 in january 2022 , khosla ventures raised $ 557 million in its first opportunity fund . [ 9 ] 
 the firm ranked first in the "founder 's choice vc " list of more than 200 venture capital firms in 2023 . [ 10 ] 
 the firm closed $ 3 . 1 billion in new capital across three funds as of november 2023 including $ 1 billion for later - stage companies , $ 500 million for seed - stage companies and $ 1 . 6 billion for its eighth flagship fund . it was the largest fundraiser by a venture capital firm that year . khosla ventures stated that the funding would be used for nuclear fusion , humanoid robots and artificial intelligence to support industries such as healthcare and transportation . [ 11 ] 
 in february 2024 , keith rabois returned to the firm as a managing director . [ 12 ] in october 2024 , the firm raised a special purpose vehicle of $ 405 million to invest in openai . [ 13 ] 
 notable investments 
 khosla ventures invests in companies in areas such as artificial intelligence , climate , sustainability , enterprise , consumer , financial technology , digital health , medical technology and diagnostics , therapeutics and frontier technology . 
 khosla ventures invested in doordash in 2013 before the company went public in 2020 with a $ 72 billion valuation . the firm also invested in instacart in 2012 as part of the seed round before going public in 2020 with $ 11 billion in market capital . other consumer investments include opendoor . [ 14 ] 
 the firm invested in okta in series b funding in 2011 before going public in 2017 and gitlab in series a funding in 2015 before going public in 2021 with in $ 15 billion market capital . other enterprise investments include cylance , rubrik , nutanix , and replit . [ 15 ] [ 16 ] [ 17 ] 
 khosla ventures invested in block , inc. 's series a funding round in 2009 before the company went public in 2015 . [ 18 ] the firm also invested affirm in its series a round in 2013 before going public in 2021 with a $ 24 billion valuation . [ 19 ] other fintech investments include stripe , upstart , and ramp . [ 20 ] 
 khosla ventures invested in commonwealth fusion 's $ 115 million series a funding round in 2019 . [ 21 ] khosla was also an early investor in quantumscape which went public in 2020 . [ 22 ] other sustainability investments include fortera , lanzatech and ver dagy . 
 the firm invested in guardant health 's series b funding round in 2014 before going public in 2018 and alivecor in 2012 . [ 23 ] other health investments include headspace , oscar , and sword health . 
 khosla ventures was the first venture capital firm to invest in openai in 2018 . [ 24 ] the firm also invested in rocket lab 's series a funding round in 2013 before going public in 2021 . [ 25 ] other frontier investments include glydways , hermeus , opentrons , and varda . 
 programs and partnerships 
 in february 2021 , khosla ventures filed plans for the public offerings of three special - purpose acquisition companies ( spac ) , which intend to raise a total of $ 1 . 2 billion for the purpose of acquiring and taking public three private companies . [ 26 ] 
 through a khosla - backed spac , nextdoor , trading under the ticker kind , had its initial public offering in november 2021 with a $ 4 . 3 billion valuation . by august 2023 kind 's market cap had fallen to about $ 810 million . [ 27 ] khosla ventures acquisition co. announced that it would close business in december 2023 . [ 28 ]

 term partnerships 
 one of the most important aspects of raising capital for your healthtech startup is managing investor relationships . investors are not just sources of funding , but also potential partners who can provide valuable guidance , feedback , and connections . however , building and maintaining long - term partnerships with investors is not easy . it requires a lot of communication , transparency , and trust . in this section , we will explore some of the best practices and tips for managing investor relationships in the healthtech industry . we will also look at some of the common challenges and pitfalls that you may encounter along the way . 
 here are some of the key points to consider when managing investor relationships : 
 1. know your investors . before you approach any investor , you should do your homework and research their background , interests , portfolio , and investment criteria . this will help you tailor your pitch and demonstrate your fit with their vision and goals . you should also try to understand their expectations , preferences , and style of communication . some investors may want frequent updates , while others may prefer less involvement . some may be more hands - on , while others may be more hands - off . knowing your investors will help you communicate effectively and avoid misunderstandings or conflicts . 
 2. keep them informed . once you have secured an investment , you should keep your investors updated on your progress , milestones , challenges , and opportunities . you should send regular reports , newsletters , or emails that highlight your achievements , metrics , and learnings . you should also share your vision , strategy , and roadmap for the future . keeping your investors informed will help you build trust and credibility , as well as solicit feedback and advice . it will also help you avoid surprises or disappointments that may damage your relationship .

 4. acknowledge their contribution . investors are not just financial supporters , but also emotional supporters . they have invested not only their money , but also their time , energy , and reputation in your startup . you should acknowledge their contribution and express your gratitude for their support . you should also celebrate your wins and achievements with them , and share your challenges and failures with them . acknowledging their contribution will help you strengthen your bond and loyalty , as well as motivate them to continue supporting you . 
 5. manage their expectations . investors are not just partners , but also stakeholders . they have invested in your startup with the expectation of getting a return on their investment . you should manage their expectations and be realistic and honest about your potential and risks . you should also communicate your milestones and goals clearly and consistently , and report your performance and results accurately and timely . you should also be proactive and transparent about any issues or problems that may affect your progress or outcome . managing their expectations will help you avoid disappointment or frustration , as well as maintain your integrity and reputation .

 one of the biggest challenges for healthtech startups is raising capital . unlike other industries , healthtech startups often face high regulatory hurdles , long development cycles , and uncertain market demand . these factors make it hard for them to attract traditional investors such as venture capitalists or angel investors , who usually look for fast returns and low risks . moreover , healthtech startups may have to give up a large share of their equity or control in exchange for funding , which can limit their future growth potential and innovation . 
 fortunately , there is a newer and safer way to raise capital for healthtech startups : safe . safe stands for simple agreement for future equity , and it is a type of contract that allows startups to receive money from investors without issuing equity or debt . instead , the investors get the right to receive equity in the future , at a discounted price , when the startup raises a priced round of funding or achieves a certain valuation . this way , the investors can benefit from the upside of the startup , while the startup can retain more ownership and flexibility . 
 safe is especially relevant for healthtech startups because it offers several advantages over other forms of financing . here are some of them : 
 1. safe is simple and fast . unlike equity or debt , safe does not require complex negotiations , valuations , or legal documents . it is based on a standard template that can be easily customized and signed online . this saves time and money for both parties , and allows the startup to focus on its core business instead of fundraising . 
 2. safe is flexible and fair . safe does not impose any interest , maturity date , or repayment obligation on the startup . it also does not dilute the existing shareholders or affect the voting rights of the founders . the startup can raise as much or as little money as it needs , from as many or as few investors as it wants , without worrying about the impact on its cap table or governance . the investors , on the other hand , can enjoy a lower entry price and a higher conversion rate than equity or debt , as well as the option to opt out of future rounds if they wish . 
 3. safe is aligned and supportive . safe aligns the interests of the 
 startup investors 
 , as both parties share the same vision and goal : the success of the startup . the investors do not have any incentive to pressure the startup to exit prematurely or to pursue short - term profits over long - term value . instead , they can provide mentorship , feedback , and connections to help the startup grow and scale . the startup can also leverage the credibility and reputation of the investors to attract more customers , partners , and talent . 
 to illustrate how safe works in practice , let us look at some examples of healthtech startups that have used it successfully : 
 - oscar health , a digital health insurance company , raised $ 165 million in a safe round in 2018 , at a $ 3 . 2 billion valuation . the round was led by founders fund , and included other prominent investors such as alphabet , khosla ventures , and thrive capital . oscar health used the funds to expand its product offerings , geographic reach , and 
 customer base 
 , and later raised another $ 375 million from alphabet at a $ 3 . 75 billion valuation . 
 - hims & hers , a telehealth platform that offers online consultations and prescriptions for various health and wellness needs , raised $ 100 million in a safe round in 2019 , at a $ 1 billion valuation . the round was led by founders fund , and included other notable investors such as forerunner ventures , ivp , redpoint ventures , and sv angel . hims & hers used the funds to launch new verticals , acquire new customers , and improve its technology and operations , and later went public via a spac merger at a $ 1 . 6 billion valuation . 
 - zocdoc , an online marketplace that connects patients with doctors and dentists , raised $ 150 million in a safe round in 2020 , at a $ 1 . 8 billion valuation . the round was led by durable capital partners , and included other existing investors such as atomico , founders fund , and khosla ventures . zocdoc used the funds to accelerate its growth , enhance its product features , and increase its market penetration , and later raised another $ 230 million at a $ 2 . 8 billion valuation . 
 these examples show that safe can be a powerful tool for healthtech startups to raise capital , without compromising their vision , values , or potential . safe can help healthtech startups overcome the challenges of fundraising , and enable them to focus on creating innovative solutions that can improve the lives and health of millions of people .

 one of the most important decisions that venture capital ( vc ) fund managers have to make is how to allocate their capital across different types of investments . there is no one - size - fits - all strategy for vc investing , as different funds may have different objectives , risk preferences , and market opportunities . however , some general principles and best practices can guide vc fund managers in designing and executing their investment strategies . in this section , we will discuss some of the key factors that influence vc investment strategies , such as fund size , stage focus , sector focus , geographic focus , diversification , and portfolio management . we will also provide some examples of successful vc funds that have adopted different investment strategies and achieved high returns for their investors . 
 - fund size : the size of a vc fund determines how much capital it can deploy and how many investments it can make . larger funds tend to invest in later - stage companies that require more capital and have higher valuations , while smaller funds tend to invest in earlier - stage companies that require less capital and have lower valuations . larger funds may also have more resources and reputation to attract and support high - quality entrepreneurs , while smaller funds may have more flexibility and agility to identify and pursue emerging opportunities . for example , sequoia capital is one of the largest and most successful vc funds in the world , with over $ 38 billion in assets under management . sequoia invests in companies across all stages , from seed to growth , and has backed some of the most iconic companies in the tech industry , such as apple , google , facebook , airbnb , and stripe . on the other hand , y combinator is one of the most influential and prolific seed - stage vc funds in the world , with over $ 3 billion in assets under management . y combinator provides seed funding , mentorship , and network to hundreds of startups every year , and has helped launch some of the most innovative and disruptive companies in the tech industry , such as dropbox , airbnb , stripe , reddit , and coinbase . 
 - stage focus : the stage of a company refers to its level of development , maturity , and traction . vc funds may specialize in investing in companies at a specific stage , such as seed , early , or late , or they may invest across multiple stages , depending on their expertise , risk appetite , and return expectations . investing in earlier - stage companies involves higher risk but also higher potential reward , as these companies have less proven business models , products , and markets , but also more room for growth and innovation . investing in later - stage companies involves lower risk but also lower potential reward , as these companies have more established business models , products , and markets , but also more competition and valuation pressure . for example , benchmark capital is a vc fund that focuses exclusively on early - stage investments , typically leading the series a round of financing for startups . benchmark has a reputation for being a hands - on and value - added partner for entrepreneurs , and has invested in some of the most successful and influential companies in the tech industry , such as ebay , twitter , uber , snapchat , and instagram . on the other hand , tiger global management is a vc fund that focuses primarily on late - stage investments , typically participating in the series d or later rounds of financing for startups . tiger global has a reputation for being a fast and aggressive investor , and has invested in some of the most valuable and high - growth companies in the tech industry , such as facebook , linkedin , spotify , flipkart , and bytedance . 
 - sector focus : the sector of a company refers to its industry , market , and domain . vc funds may specialize in investing in companies in a specific sector , such as software , biotechnology , or e - commerce , or they may invest across multiple sectors , depending on their expertise , interest , and opportunity . investing in a specific sector allows vc funds to develop deep knowledge , network , and reputation in that sector , and to identify and support the best entrepreneurs and innovations in that sector . investing across multiple sectors allows vc funds to diversify their portfolio , access a wider range of opportunities , and leverage cross - sector synergies and learnings . for example , andreessen horowitz is a vc fund that invests across multiple sectors , such as software , internet , media , e - commerce , fintech , biotech , and crypto . andreessen horowitz has a team of experts , advisors , and operators in each sector , and provides comprehensive support and resources to its portfolio companies . andreessen horowitz has invested in some of the most transformative and visionary companies in the tech industry , such as facebook , airbnb , slack , coinbase , and instacart . on the other hand , khosla ventures is a vc fund that invests primarily in companies in the biotechnology and clean technology sectors , such as synthetic biology , gene editing , renewable energy , and climate change . khosla ventures has a mission to support entrepreneurs who are tackling the biggest challenges and opportunities in human and planetary health , and has invested in some of the most innovative and impactful companies in the tech industry , such as 23 and me , editas medicine , impossible foods , and lanzatech .

# U.S. Housing Market 2025: Commercial Rationale and Investment Analysis  

---  

## Executive Summary  
The U.S. housing market in 2025 presents a complex landscape shaped by affordability challenges, regional disparities, and structural supply shortages. Key trends include moderated price growth (2-3% annually), a housing shortage estimated at 2.5–5.25 million units, and elevated mortgage rates constraining buyer demand 【1】【3】【4】. While national inventory remains tight, regional markets like Cleveland and Kansas City demonstrate resilience due to affordability, creating arbitrage opportunities for investors 【2】【6】. Projections indicate the market will grow from $52.14 trillion in 2025 to $72.88 trillion by 2032 at a 4.9% CAGR, driven by single-family homes and multifamily rentals 【4】【7】.  

---  

## Market Dynamics and Structural Challenges  

### Supply-Demand Imbalance  
The U.S. faces a severe housing shortage caused by stagnant new construction and low existing inventory. Barriers include high land costs, regulatory hurdles, labor shortages, and inflation-driven construction expenses 【3】【9】. Existing homeowners with low mortgage rates are reluctant to sell, exacerbating inventory constraints 【4】【6】.  

### Affordability Crisis  
High home prices and mortgage rates (elevated since 2022) have suppressed demand, particularly for first-time buyers. This has led to a "lock-in" effect, where homeowners remain in their properties to avoid refinancing at higher rates 【6】【9】.  

### Economic and Monetary Factors  
Interest rates and inflation remain critical determinants. The Federal Reserve’s "higher-for-longer" rate policy has dampened market activity, while GDP growth and consumer confidence will influence future demand 【1】【5】【8】.  

---  

## Regional Disparities and Investment Opportunities  

| Region          | Affordability | Price Trends  | Inventory | Investment Potential |  
|-----------------|---------------|---------------|-----------|----------------------|  
| Midwest (Cleveland, Kansas City) | High          | Stable/Growth | Moderate  | High (Arbitrage)     |  
| South (Texas, Florida)          | Low           | Decline       | High      | Moderate             |  
| West Coast      | Very Low      | Decline       | High      | Low (Risk)           |  

Regional markets with affordability, such as the Midwest, are expected to outperform. Investors leveraging hyper-local data can capitalize on undervalued properties in these areas 【2】【4】【7】.  

---  

## Financial Projection Methodologies  

1. **Supply-Demand Analysis**: Quantifying housing shortages using Census Bureau data and construction metrics 【3】.  
2. **Cap Rate Evaluation**: Balancing return and risk, as high cap rates in distressed markets may signal higher default risks 【2】.  
3. **Macroeconomic Modeling**: Assessing GDP growth, inflation, and interest rate trajectories to forecast market cycles 【5】【9】.  
4. **Regional Comparative Analysis**: Identifying markets with favorable price-to-income ratios and demographic tailwinds 【4】【6】.  

---  

## Success Criteria for Investors  

| Factor                | Description                                                                 |  
|-----------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|  
| **Affordability Focus** | Target regions with stable or improving price-to-income ratios 【2】【7】. |  
| **Inventory Timing**   | Leverage low inventory in entry-level markets to secure off-market deals 【4】. |  
| **Risk Mitigation**    | Avoid high-cost regions with declining demand and rising vacancies 【6】【9】. |  
| **Long-Term Leverage** | Position for growth in multifamily rentals and single-family rentals (SFRs) 【7】【4】. |  

---  

## Challenges and Constraints  
- **Persistent High Rates**: Mortgage rates above 6% remain a drag on buyer activity 【1】【6】.  
- **Construction Barriers**: Regulatory and cost challenges delay new housing supply 【3】【9】.  
- **Economic Uncertainty**: A potential recession or prolonged inflation could further depress market confidence 【5】【8】.  

---  

## Conclusion  
Participation in the 2025 U.S. housing market requires a nuanced, data-driven approach. While national trends suggest moderation, regional opportunities—particularly in affordable Midwestern markets—offer a compelling risk-adjusted return. Investors must prioritize affordability metrics, regional specialization, and long-term occupancy strategies to navigate the current landscape effectively 【2】【4】【7】.  

---  

*Note: All projections and analyses are based on data available as of June 2025. Market conditions may evolve rapidly due to unforeseen economic or regulatory changes.*

1.title: US Housing Market Forecast and Analysis 2025 – 2027
1.content:
us housing market forecast and analysis 2025 – 2027 
 david garner 
 published on : june 13 th , 2025 
 us housing market forecast : 2025 - 2027 outlook 
 published on : june 13 th , 2025 
 understanding the trajectory of the u.s. housing market is paramount for both prospective homeowners and property investors . for international investors and domestic buyers alike , future market movements directly impact investment viability , potential returns , and strategic planning . as we navigate economic landscape dogged by uncertainty , looking ahead to 2025 , 2026 , and 2027 provides crucial foresight for making informed decisions today . 
 this article delves into the latest housing market predictions from leading financial institutions , offering an in - depth analysis of the factors driving these forecasts . we ’ll explore the evolving affordability crisis , regional market variances , and how these shifts present unique opportunities for investors looking to refine their acquisition strategies and underwriting practices . 
 key takeaways : 
 moderated price growth : overall u.s. home price growth is expected to slow down significantly in 2025 - 2026 compared to recent years , averaging 2 - 3 % annually , with some forecasts predicting slight declines on a national average basis . 
 affordability crisis : high home prices combined with elevated mortgage rates are the primary deterrents for buyers , leading to reduced demand and increasing inventory in some markets . 
 rising inventory : the supply of homes for sale is improving nationally , offering more options for buyers , though still below pre - pandemic “ normal ” levels in some more affordable markets . 
 regional divergence : significant variations exist ; while some sun belt states ( e . g . , florida , texas , louisiana , california ) are seeing price drops and increased inventory , metro areas in the midwest and northeast are often experiencing continued price increases due to persistent demand and tighter supply . 
 investor opportunity : the shifting market favours an investment strategy that prioritizes regional nuances , emphasizing due diligence , competitive pricing , conservative underwriting , and a focus on long - term cash flow and appreciation in stable or growing markets . 
 current housing market snapshot ( early - mid 2025 ) 
 as of early to mid - 2025 , the u.s. housing mark entered a cycle rebalancing . after years of rapid appreciation , driven by low interest rates and limited supply , the market is now grappling with challenges to affordability . 
 the median u.s. home price has reached record highs , making homeownership a significant hurdle for many . this is compounded by elevated mortgage rates , which , despite daily fluctuations , remain substantially higher than the historically low rates seen just a few years ago . 
 current mortgage rate landscape ( as of june 12 , 2025 ) : 
 mortgage type national average apr ( june 12 , 2025 ) weekly change 
 30-year fixed 6 . 88 % - 0 . 11 % 
 15-year fixed 5 . 94 % - 0 . 12 % 
 5-year arm 7 . 21 % - 0 . 41 % 
 data source : zillow 
 commentary : the elevated cost of borrowing , combined with high home prices , has led to a noticeable cooling in buyer demand across many segments of the market . 
 housing market forecasts : 2025 - 2027 predictions 
 leading institutions and housing market experts offer varying but generally aligned predictions for the u.s. housing market in the coming years , pointing towards a period of moderation and potential rebalancing . 
 home price growth predictions ( national – panel mean cumulative % change from q4 2024 ) : 
 year ( end of ) projected cumulative % change 
 2025 + 3 . 4 % 
 2026 + 6 . 8 % 
 2027 + 10 . 8 % 
 data source : reuters 
 commentary : while the “ crazy - high price jumps ” of recent years are expected to cool , the consensus among experts still predicts a steady , albeit slower , climb . for 2025 , the average forecast is for national home prices to increase by approximately 3 . 4 % . this moderates slightly from earlier projections , reflecting persistent inflation and somewhat elevated mortgage rates . 
 looking further ahead , cumulative gains of nearly 7% by end of 2026 and over 10 % by end of 2027 are anticipated . however , some individual forecasts , like zillow ’ s , project a slight national dip of 0 . 9 % between april 2025 and april 2026 , marking a more bearish stance . this diversity highlights the inherent uncertainty but underscores a general shift away from rapid , unsustainable appreciation . 
 key factors driving market shifts & forecasts 
 the projected moderation and regional divergences in the housing market are primarily driven by the following interconnected factors : 
 housing affordability ( main reason for slowdown ) : this is the paramount issue . high home prices , coupled with elevated mortgage rates , have significantly eroded purchasing power for both first - time buyers and many existing homeowners . a substantial portion of u.s. households are currently priced out of the median - priced home market . the income - to - mortgage ratio has reached critical levels , making monthly payments unsustainable for a large segment of potential buyers . 
 building inventory : as buyer demand cools due to affordability constraints , the supply of homes for sale is gradually increasing . this shift from a severe seller ’s market to a more balanced environment provides buyers with more options and negotiating power . in some regions , inventory is “ skyrocketing past pre - covid levels , ” signalling a notable supply surplus . 
 shifting buyer demand : the intense buyer competition of recent years has normalized . with more choices and less urgency , buyers are becoming more cautious and price - sensitive . this directly contributes to prices falling in certain markets and slower appreciation nationally . 
 mortgage rate volatility : while the overall trend for rates is expected to be stable to slightly decreasing ( as discussed in our daily mortgage updates and 2026 - 2027 mortgage rate forecasts ) , their current elevated levels significantly impact buyer budgets . 
 economic conditions : broader economic factors like inflation trends , labour market stability , and consumer confidence play a crucial role . any signs of an economic slowdown can make potential home buyers pause on major financial decisions . 
 regional variance : a fragmented market 
 you may have heard the term “ real estate is local ” . well , the “ national average ” numbers thrown around in the headlines often mask significant regional differences . the u.s. housing market in 2025 is deeply fragmented , with a clear divergence in price trends across different geographies . 
 markets seeing price drops / cooling : 
 florida , texas , louisiana , and california : these states , particularly certain counties and metro areas within them , are experiencing significant price declines and/or rising inventory . for instance , areas in florida ( e . g . , cape coral , punta gorda , naples , north port ) and texas ( e . g . , mcallen , victoria , waco , eagle pass ) have reported negative year - over - year price growth in early 2025 . this often occurs in areas that saw massive , rapid price surges during the pandemic due to migration influx or speculative investing , and are now undergoing a correction . louisiana also shows areas with declining values ( e . g . , lake charles , alexandria , houma ) . in california , high - priced coastal counties like san francisco and santa clara are seeing declines due to affordability constraints and shifting migration patterns . 
 reasoning : these regions frequently experience oversupply ( especially new construction ) , affordability challenges , and a reversal of pandemic - era migration trends as people are recalled to workplaces in major metros . 
 markets still seeing price rises / resilience : 
 midwest and northeast metro areas : in stark contrast , many metro areas in the midwest ( e . g . , kokomo , in ; decatur , il ; muskegon , mi ; lima , oh ; evansville , in ; battle creek , mi ) and northeast ( e . g . , syracuse , ny ; weirton , wv ; new haven , ct ; vineland , nj ) are demonstrating notable resilience , with consistent price increases and even double - digit growth in some pockets . 
 reasoning : these markets often continue to benefit from relatively better affordability , stable local economies , and less aggressive overbuilding during the pandemic , leading to persistent demand outstripping current inventory levels . 
 commentary : this fragmentation underscores that real estate is fundamentally local . a national forecast provides a general direction , but successful investment hinges on understanding the specific dynamics of individual markets . 
 implications for investors : adjusting your strategy 
 the current and forecasted u.s. housing market conditions present both challenges and significant opportunities for property investors , particularly for our international investors . the key is to adjust investment strategy and underwriting to reflect these shifts . 
 where investors should look to buy : 
 affordable growth markets ( midwest / northeast ) : focus on metro areas in the midwest and northeast that are still experiencing steady , single - digit price appreciation and healthy rental demand . these markets offer potentially more stable returns and less risk of immediate price corrections . they represent undervalued opportunities . 
 correction markets with long - term potential ( sun belt ) : for higher - risk , higher - reward strategies , consider areas in texas , florida , and other sun belt states where prices have seen significant declines . these markets may offer “ heavy discounts ” for buyers . however , this requires a deeper understanding of local demand drivers and patience for potential recovery . 
 focus on cash flow : regardless of location , prioritize properties that offer strong cash flow from rental income , especially in a higher - interest - rate environment . look for a healthy debt service coverage ratio ( dscr ) . 
 undervalued metros : actively seek out areas where current pricing may not fully reflect long - term growth potential or where affordability has improved , leading to renewed buyer interest . 
 advantages and benefits in current market conditions : 
 increased inventory = more choice : unlike the frenzy of recent years , rising inventory means investors have more properties to choose from and less competition , allowing for more thorough due diligence . 
 negotiating power : with softening demand and increasing supply in many areas , buyers now have more leverage to negotiate on price , terms , and even seller concessions . this is a significant advantage for securing better deals . 
 moderating prices : even if national prices aren’t crashing , the slowdown in appreciation or outright drops in certain regions means you can enter the market at more reasonable price points , potentially improving your long - term return on investment ( roi ) . 
 focus on fundamentals : the current market forces investors to return to fundamental real estate principles : strong local economies , population growth , job creation , and solid rental demand , rather than relying solely on rapid appreciation . 
 adjusting investment strategy and underwriting : 
 conservative underwriting : adopt more conservative underwriting assumptions , particularly regarding future rent growth and potential vacancy rates . build in larger buffers for unexpected expenses . 
 focus on debt service coverage : given persistent mortgage rates , rigorously evaluate the dscr for investment properties . ensure the property ’s income can comfortably cover the mortgage payment and operating expenses . 
 long - term horizon : emphasize a long - term hold strategy . short - term fluctuations are normal in a transitioning market ; patient investors focused on long - term equity growth and consistent cash flow will fare best . 
 deep market research : conduct exhaustive research into local market conditions . national trends are only a guide ; understanding hyper - local supply - demand dynamics , job markets , and demographic shifts is critical . 
 stress testing : stress test your investment pro - formas with slightly higher interest rates or lower rental incomes to ensure the deal remains viable under less - than - ideal conditions . 
 capital reserves : maintain adequate capital reserves to cover potential vacancies , maintenance , or unexpected costs , especially if interest rates remain elevated or if the market experiences further shifts . 
 conclusion 
 the u.s. housing market forecast for 2025 - 2027 points towards a period of moderation , driven by affordability challenges and increasing inventory , but with significant regional variances . while this transition presents headwinds for some , it creates strategic opportunities for discerning property investors . 
 by understanding these evolving dynamics , focusing on robust underwriting , prioritizing cash flow , and strategically targeting markets with strong fundamentals or attractive discounts , international investors can navigate this complex environment successfully . as always , consulting with experienced real estate and financial professionals is paramount to tailoring these strategies to your specific goals and circumstances .

2.title: Unlocking Value in America’s Uneven Housing Markets
2.content:
unlocking value in america ’s uneven housing markets 
 david garner 
 published on : may 22 nd , 2025 
 when i started investing in u.s. real estate as a foreigner in 2016 , i quickly realized how important regional nuance is when it comes to housing market data . 
 after acquiring over 120 investment properties , i ’ve developed a hyper - local data - driven approach that cuts through the noise of national housing statistics to find genuine value . 
 why regional disparities matter 
 supply and demand dictates the price of all assets , and affordability drives demand for housing more than almost any other factor . this fundamental truth creates predictable patterns across america ’s fragmented housing landscape . 
 recent forecasts from zillow confirm what i ’ve observed first - hand : midwest regions with affordable housing like cleveland and kansas city will avoid the price declines expected in less affordable markets like texas , louisiana , and florida . 
 the logic is straightforward . people buy homes where they can afford them . 
 when affordability deteriorates , demand falls and supply increases , adding downward pressure to houses prices . this creates a natural arbitrage opportunity for investors who understand these regional dynamics . 
 quantifying risk and return 
 many foreign investors make the mistake of chasing the highest cap rates without understanding the associated risks . 
 cap rate isn’t just a measure of return , it ’s a measure of risk . 
 properties with cap rates exceeding 10 % often come with exponentially higher chances of rent delinquencies and property damage . these d - class assets attract d - class tenants with much higher default risks and a plethora of social problems . 
 through years of experience , i ’ve found the sweet spot lies between 7 - 10 % cap rates . 
 this range typically allows properties to generate positive cash flow while limiting the operational headaches that erode actual returns . it provides a buffer to ride out market fluctuations while building equity through mortgage paydown regardless of market conditions . 
 future - proofing your investment 
 the most successful investments i ’ve made focus on “ future - proofing ” properties through high quality renovations . 
 addressing big - ticket infrastructure items upfront like the roof , wiring , plumbing , sewer lines , furnace , and hvac prevents costly repairs and replcements later . a $ 10 , 000 roof replacement or $ 20 , 000 sewer line excavation can quickly erase years of positive cash flow . 
 quality internal remodels with new kitchens and bathrooms attract better tenants who pay on time and stay longer . 
 this approach might mean paying more upfront , but it dramatically reduces vacancy rates , delinquencies , repairs , and capital expenditures over time . 
 our goal should be to treat a property like an asset , not an atm . build up cash reserves for improvements to add value , and/or for additional mortgage payments . making just one extra mortgage payment per year can reduce the life of your mortgage by 4 or 5 years . 
 the foreign investor advantage 
 as foreign investors buying from a distance , we have an unexpected edge : emotional detachment . 
 we rely heavily on data , which facilitates more objective decision - making than local investors who might be influenced by personal biases or market narratives . 
 tools like corelogic and attom provide accurate , hyperlocal , current , and accessible data that reveal opportunities others might miss by just ‘ walking the street ’ . 
 of course , this data - driven approach must be paired with a strong local team that provides physical presence and valuable local market expertise . real estate is local , and even within a specific neighbourhood there are good streets and bad streets . that local market expertise is like the cherry on the cake when it comes to identifying a good deal vs a bad one . 
 case study : cleveland success 
 recently , we helped a client close on an investment property in cleveland that perfectly illustrates these principles . 
 our data analysis showed people moving into the neighborhood , with population rising within a 1-3 mile radius . vacancy rates were falling , homeownership was increasing , and rental listings were taking 50 + applications within days of hitting the market . 
 but because local buyers were hesitating – mostly due to interest rate uncertainty – we were able to negotiate a significant seller concession that covered all of our clients closing costs and paid for a mortgage rate buydown of 1 % . 
 this improved monthly cash flow , saved approximately $ 36 , 000 in mortgage interest over the loan term , and potentially help to reduce our clients income tax liability . 
 at the end of the day , market uncertainty means some local buyers try and wait it out , and that creates leverage for investors at the negotiation table . 
 overcoming remote investment challenges 
 the biggest challenge foreign investors looking at a property investment in the usa is building the local network needed for proper due diligence and property management . 
 successful real estate investment requires coordinating realtors , home inspectors , property managers , attorneys , title companies , insurance agents , contractors , and appraisers . this is difficult to assemble for just one or two properties and even harder to coordinate from overseas . 
 at cash flow rentals , we’ve developed a systematic approach to remote due diligence based on our own experience building our personal portfolio : 
 phase 1 combines arms - length property evaluation with physical on - site inspection . 
 post - contract , we commission multiple independent inspections and an appraisal to ensure we ’re not overpaying or buying hidden problems . 
 this systematic approach has proven effective across hundreds of transactions for both our own portfolio and our clients . 
 capital requirements and financing strategy 
 i ’m cautious about over leveraging . while financing is our best tool for maximizing roi over the long - term , negative cash flow can quickly derail an investment . 
 real estate should pay for itself over time . 
 i typically recommend a 30 % down payment to create an equity buffer and ensure positive cash flow with a comfortable margin . 
 the client mentioned earlier invested approximately $ 40 , 000 cash into the deal that now generates over $ 300 monthly in positive cash flow after all operating costs and debt service . for most foreign investors , i suggest budgeting around $ 60 , 000 ( including down payment and closing costs ) for a $ 175 , 000 property . 
 that ’s based on using a foreign national mortgage like a dscr loan . 
 evolution of strategy 
 my investment approach in the us property market has evolved significantly over the years . 
 when i first started , i chased cash flow by buying lower - value homes with high rental yields . in retrospect , this was a mistake . 
 these deals looked great on spreadsheets but rarely performed as expected . they attracted problematic tenants , caused frequent evictions , and generated substantial turnover costs that destroyed projected cash flow . 
 these properties also appreciated poorly and proved difficult to sell since home buyers avoided those neighborhoods . 
 my most profitable investments have been fully renovated houses in better working - class neighborhoods with quality renovations held for the long term . 
 this strategy attracts tenants who pay on time and stay longer , limits operational costs , and generates more consistent cash flow . the properties appreciate more reliably , creating a “ double whammy ” of equity growth with far less management hassle . 
 current market analysis shows midwest properties trading at cap rates 100 + basis points higher than comparable coastal properties , confirming the regional value disparities i ’ve been capitalizing on for years . 
 current opportunities 
 today , the most compelling investment opportunities exist in northeast and midwest markets where housing affordability remains within reach for homebuyers . 
 strong job markets in these regions are attracting inward migration , driving demand from both renters and buyers . 
 the fundamentals that have guided my investment success for years remain unchanged : focus on economic and demographic trends at the regional and neighborhood level rather than broad housing market statistics . 
 this approach has allowed me to build a portfolio of over 120 properties that consistently outperform the market , and it can work for other foreign investors willing to embrace data - driven objectivity and systematic due diligence .

3.title: Navigating the U.S. Housing Shortage and Investment Implications | J.P. Morgan Asset Management

fixed income blog 
 navigating the u.s. housing shortage and investment implications 
 andrew kazior , danial qureshi , lutz schloegl 
 24 / 07 / 2025 
 introduction 
 the united states is facing a significant housing shortage , marked by a pronounced imbalance between supply and demand . our proprietary analysis , a joint effort by our portfolio management , securitized credit research , and quantitative research teams , estimates this shortage to be between 2.5 and 5.25 million units , depending on the starting point of analysis . new home construction has not kept pace with demand due to high land costs , regulatory challenges , labor shortages , and escalating construction expenses . this supply constraint is exacerbated by low existing inventory levels , as current homeowners , particularly those with low mortgage rates , are hesitant to sell . on the demand side , factors such as population growth and increased household formation , driven by immigration and demographic shifts , have intensified the need for housing . the resulting scarcity of affordable housing options , coupled with rising home prices and rental costs , underscores the challenges in meeting the housing needs of middle - and lower - income families and strengthens our positive fundamental outlook on single and multifamily residential exposure . 
 inputs & measurement 
 to assess the housing shortage in the united states , we examine supply and demand metrics provided by the census bureau . on the supply side , we consider the completion of new residential housing units and the shipment of new manufactured units , while also accounting for the loss or retirement of existing housing stock . on the demand side , household formations serve as the primary inputs . this process involves the creation of new households through marriage , divorce , leaving the parental home , migration , or changes in economic conditions . the data is primarily sourced from the decennial comprehensive count by the census bureau and supplemented by more frequent surveys . during the pandemic period ( 2020 q2 and q 3 ) , a haircut factor is applied to mitigate the noise introduced when the census bureau suspended in - person data collection and switched to telephone interviews . by comparing these supply and demand metrics at both national and regional levels , we can quantify the extent of the housing shortage and identify trends over time . 
 results 
 the measurement of the housing shortage is highly dependent on the starting point of analysis . using 2001 as a baseline , the shortage is estimated at 2.5 million units , whereas starting in 2012 shows a larger deficit of 5.25 million units . this variation highlights how the baseline year affects the perceived extent of the shortage . leading up to and immediately following the global financial crisis ( gfc ) , the housing market had a surplus due to overbuilding and the decline in the formation of households as living arrangements changed . however , that surplus quickly diminished as demand surged due to improved economic conditions , millennials entering peak household formation ages , and baby boomers continuing to hold a growing stock of homes . the pandemic further fueled this trend , with consumers experiencing greater wealth accumulation and additional socio - economic changes . no matter the timeline , it ’s clear the united states is facing a mismatch between supply and demand . 
 implications 
 the housing shortage in the united states is poised to continue , fueled by persistent demographic trends and ongoing under building . with robust population growth , especially in regions like the south where significant population influxes account for over half of the national shortage , the demand for housing is expected to consistently surpass supply . the k - shaped consumer economic recovery , marked by higher income brackets accumulating wealth and potentially purchasing multiple homes , further intensifies the national shortage by restricting housing availability for middle - and lower - income families . this trend is likely to continue . the shortage may be even larger than our calculation , as it ’s been estimated that household formations may be understated by up to 0.4 million because of ' missing ' households that did not form due to the lack of available housing units . shifting to investment implications , the current housing shortage reinforces our positive fundamental outlook surrounding single and multifamily housing exposure . opportunities in securitized credit , such as single - family rentals , credit risk transfers , and residential transition loans remain attractive , offering effective financing solutions to meet the housing needs of various income groups .

 u.s. housing market driver - population growth in sun belt and midwest regions 
 the population growth in the sun belt and midwest regions of the u.s. has been a key driver of the u.s. housing market over the past decade . warm weather locations in states like florida , texas , arizona , and nevada as well as midwestern regions such as north carolina , south carolina , tennessee and colorado have seen significant increases in population as people relocate from more northern parts of the country . according to the u.s. census bureau , texas added over 470 , 000 new residents in 2023 , the largest numeric increase of any u.s. state . 
 this influx has put pressure on the supply of housing in these areas , pushing prices higher . home builders have ramped up new construction to meet the rising demand from incoming residents . strong job growth in various industries such as services , technology and manufacturing have made these sun belt and midwestern regions attractive places for individuals and families to put down roots . the warmer climates and relatively lower costs of living compared to the west and northeast coastal cities have also contributed to the population shifts to these parts of the country , fueling housing market activity . 
 u.s. housing market opportunity - expansion of build - to - rent housing models 
 one opportunity emerging for the u.s housing market is the expansion of build - to - rent communities and housing models . large institutional investors and developers are increasingly focusing on building entire communities with rental apartments and single - family homes specifically aimed at addressing the needs of renters . this provides welcome supply in the rental market as more young professionals and households choose not to buy homes and rent for longer periods . the build - to - rent projects are often completed quickly in contrast to traditional builder - developed subdivisions . they offer attractive amenities and services aligned to renters ’ preferences . as mortgage rates remain elevated , renting also looks a relatively affordable option for many potential homeowners , helping boost the demand for these new build - to - rent communities . this emerging model is well - placed to benefit from demographic and housing demand trends in the coming years .

5.title: What Housing Trends Reveal About the Economy
5.content:
what housing trends reveal about the economy 
 07 / 15 / 2025 
 felipe moraes 
 housing markets act as both mirror and motor for the broader economy , reflecting shifts in consumer confidence , financial conditions , and regulatory climates . by examining home prices , inventory levels , lending trends , and buyer behavior , we can piece together a comprehensive picture of economic health and trajectory . in this detailed exploration , we unpack the most current data as of mid - 2025 , highlighting practical insights for prospective homeowners , policymakers , and industry professionals seeking to navigate an evolving landscape . 
 understanding the macroeconomic backdrop 
 the u.s. economy entered 2025 on a path of tempered growth . with nominal gdp reaching $ 29 . 37 trillion in q3 2024 , output remains robust compared to historical norms . yet beneath that headline strength lies a nuanced narrative . unemployment stood at 4 . 1 % at the end of 2024 , signaling resilient labor market conditions even as inflation pressures persisted . 
 consumer prices climbed 2 . 9 % year - over - year by december 2024 , indicating that inflation is present but not runaway . federal reserve guidance and market expectations point to a “ higher - for - longer ” interest rate regime , suggesting that borrowing costs may stay elevated well into 2025 . against this backdrop , economic growth is forecast to continue at a moderate pace — slower than the rapid post - pandemic rebound but still positive and supportive of housing demand . 
 shifts in home prices and affordability 
 after surging in the early 2020 s , home price appreciation has decelerated . forecasts for 2025 estimate average growth of 2 – 3 % in home values , down from nearly 4 . 5 % in 2024 . indeed , may 2025 ’s year - over - year increase of 2 . 5 % marked the second - lowest reading in aei ’s multi - decade series , compared to 5 . 4 % one year prior . 
 even as growth moderates , affordability remains a pressing concern . mortgage rates near 7% and home prices at or above previous peaks mean the cost of ownership is still out of reach for many . young and first - time buyers , in particular , face the twin challenges of high down payments and elevated debt service burdens . this dynamic has prompted more households to consider sharing space , delaying purchases , or prioritizing renovations over relocation . 
 mortgage rates and lending activity 
 mortgage rates , having dipped to around 6 . 2 % in late 2024 , climbed back above 7% in early 2025 and hovered at 6 . 94 % by late may . while these levels are elevated by historical standards , they remain slightly lower than peaks earlier in the tightening cycle , providing some relief to borrowing costs . 
 as rates settle in the high 6 – 7 % range for most of 2025 , refinance activity is expected to edge upward , and purchase origination may tick higher as buyers adjust their expectations . yet persistently high mortgage rates continue to limit qualifying power , leading many potential homeowners to pause until market conditions improve or until they can secure a more favorable financing package . 
 inventory , supply , and home construction 
 supply shortages that once plagued the market are showing signs of easing , but a fully balanced market remains elusive . nationally , single - family existing home listings rose approximately 20 % year - over - year , yet inventory still lags 20 – 30 % below prior troughs . new home supply , at 481 , 000 units , reached its highest level since 2007 , and speculative homes for sale topped 385 , 000 , the most since 2008 . 
 meanwhile , construction activity is recovering from pandemic - era disruptions but faces its own hurdles . material costs , labor shortages , and stringent regulations have tempered builder enthusiasm . with home price growth slowing , some developers are pulling back , opting to fill existing pipelines rather than embark on new projects . 
 home buyer and seller behavior 
 high costs and elevated borrowing rates have kept buyer activity subdued , even as the broader economy expands . many homeowners are “ locked in ” to mortgages with rates several percentage points below today ’s levels , diminishing their incentive to trade up or relocate . at the same time , renovation spending has surged , as homeowners invest in improvements to maximize equity gains and avoid moving . 
 muted purchase activity among first - time buyers 
 record renovation and home - improvement spending 
 reduced turnover from rate - locked sellers 
 together , these factors contribute to a market where supply remains constrained even as demand signals soften , creating pockets of opportunity in select regions and price tiers . 
 housing as an economic barometer 
 housing trends often presage shifts in the broader economy . rising home values boost consumer confidence and wealth effects , fueling spending in areas such as home furnishings , appliances , and services . this a critical gdp component underscores housing ’s outsized influence on overall economic performance . 
 conversely , a cooling or contracting market can signal waning demand , tighter credit conditions , or broader financial stress . monitoring metrics like building permits , mortgage applications , and existing - home sales provides real - time insight into consumer sentiment and the health of credit markets . 
 risks and uncertainties 
 several potential headwinds could reshape the housing outlook in 2025 and beyond . interest rate trajectories remain uncertain , hinging on inflation data , labor market resilience , and fed policy decisions . meanwhile , political transitions and policy changes — such as adjustments to tax law , zoning reform , or infrastructure spending — could introduce new volatility into both supply and demand .

 practical steps for home buyers and policymakers 
 for prospective buyers , staying informed and flexible is paramount . monitoring rate movements , prequalifying early , and expanding search criteria can uncover unexpected opportunities . exploring renovation or conversion projects may also yield cost - effective paths to ownership in competitive markets . 
 build a buffer for rate fluctuations 
 consider alternative locations or property types 
 leverage improvement incentives when available 
 policymakers and industry leaders should prioritize measures that enhance supply responsiveness — streamlining approvals , incentivizing workforce development in construction trades , and targeting support to first - time and moderate - income buyers . by doing so , they can empower informed decision - making and foster a more resilient market . 
 conclusion 
 housing trends serve as both a reflection of economic realities and a catalyst for consumer behavior . as prices stabilize , rates moderate , and inventory slowly improves , participants across the spectrum have opportunities to adapt , invest , and plan for the future . by understanding the intricate links between housing statistics and macroeconomic forces , stakeholders can anticipate challenges , seize emerging prospects , and contribute to sustainable growth in the years ahead .

u.s. housing market : a nationwide overview 
 published on april 28 , 2025 | 4 min read 
 momo productions / getty images ; illustration by austin courregé / bankrate

 faqs 
 housing affordability has been top - of - mind for buyers and sellers since mortgage rates started ratcheting up in 2022. a persistent lock - in effect is still keeping many existing homeowners unwilling or unable to sell — which makes sense , when the rate to buy your next home will be double your current rate . 
 “ one word commonly used to describe the economy is uncertainty , ” says mark hamrick , bankrate ’s senior economic analyst . “ that quality undermines confidence , particularly when we ’re talking about the biggest , most consequential purchases of a lifetime — namely , buying a home . at the same time , life can dictate the need to buy or sell based on our unique personal situation . ” 
 uncertainty undermines confidence , particularly when we ’re talking about the biggest purchase of a lifetime — buying a home . 
 — mark hamrick , bankrate senior economic analyst 
 that economic uncertainty could leave mortgage rates stuck in 2025 , experts say . what could these elevated rates , coupled with rising home prices , mean for the u.s. housing market in 2025 ? here ’s how the data breaks down . 
 key factors driving the u.s. housing market 
 record - breaking high prices : in march , sale prices of existing homes rose by 2.7 percent from the previous year , marking an all - time high for march prices and the 21st consecutive month of year - over - year increases , according to the national association of realtors ( nar ) . 
 stubbornly low inventory : at the same time , the available inventory of existing homes for sale has been too low to meet demand for quite a while . it remained so in march , despite a sizable year - over - year increase per nar , with a 4-month supply — 5 or 6 months is typically required for a balanced market . 
 still - elevated mortgage rates : the average rate for a 30-year fixed mortgage also remain stubborn , dipping back below 7 percent but not by much . as of late april , the average was 6.86 percent , according to bankrate ’s weekly survey of large lenders . 
 new construction is a mixed bag : the pace of new construction has not been fast enough to meaningfully ease the housing shortage . housing starts , a metric that measures the beginning of construction on a new residential home , fell by 11.4 percent month - over - month in march 2025 , according to the u.s. census bureau . while this is a 1.9 percent increase over march of last year , many experts anticipate new construction to be hampered by tariffs and labor shortages in the near future . on the plus side , the national association of home builders reported a healthy 8 . 9 - month supply of new homes in february 2025 . 
 local markets have their own dynamics 
 local market conditions can vary widely by region , state or even individual city . the disparities mean that your money can go much further in some markets than in others . 
 “everything ’s local — everything ’s this local supply - and - demand dynamic , ” says peter carroll , executive vp of public policy and industry relations for cotality , a real estate data firm . according to carroll , this could be due to things like natural disasters , as well as layoffs from major area employers . 
 another example of a local trend is flat or declining home prices along the gulf coast , says mike fratantoni , chief economist of the mortgage bankers association . that includes places in states like texas and florida , which have both seen large migrations in recent years . 
 “that ’s where an actually fairly robust amount of inventory is available , ” fratantoni says . “ for buyers in those markets , there are some real opportunities . ” 
 navigating the current housing market 
 thinking of buying or selling a home soon ? your experience will vary based on a wide variety of factors . home prices and mortgage rates are already high , and taxes and homeowners insurance rates are climbing , too . all of these eat into homebuyers ’ purchasing power , and make it harder for sellers to find qualified buyers . 
 while experts predict that the market will cool down eventually , they ’re relatively confident that there will not be a housing market crash akin to the great recession in the 2000 s . this is partially due to today ’s much stricter mortgage requirements . 
 the undersupply of single - family starter homes is 1.6 million units and growing . 
 the types of homes available add another layer to the housing market . some housing types are more in - demand than others : “ on a national basis , we put the undersupply of single - family starter homes at 1.6 million units and growing , ” says carroll . factors like tariffs and economic uncertainty could provide extra headwinds in constructing more affordable homes , he adds . buyers willing to consider a condo or townhouse may be able to get into homeownership at a lower price point . 
 on the whole , sellers still have the upper hand in most of the country — but that can range wildly from one geographic location to another . “ depending on the market , location and price point , sellers could find either multiple offers or the need to be flexible on price , ” says hamrick . 
 should i buy a house now or wait ? 
 is now a good time to buy a house ? whether to buy now or wait is a big decision that depends a lot on your personal circumstances . yes , mortgage rates are currently high , but days - on - market figures are up too , giving you more time to make an informed decision . and there ’s no guarantee things will improve if you hold off . 
 ultimately , deciding to buy a home is a display of confidence in your own finances . affordability continues to be an issue , but for those who can buy right now , you may see more opportunity than in recent years . 
 the overall number of homes for sale was up 15 percent year - over - year in march 2025 , according to redfin data . this could mean that you have more choices — and less competition — when it comes to your home purchase . 
 should i sell my house now or wait ? 
 low existing - home inventory levels give sellers the upper hand in most of the u.s. but with mortgage rates and prices remaining elevated , buyers are wary — which makes selling more challenging . 
 with that in mind , deciding whether now is a good time to sell your house can be tricky . again , it depends on a number of personal factors . selling may be a good idea if you ’re ready to downsize or retire , or if you need to relocate . but if you’ll then need to buy a new house , the tables will be turned and you’ll be facing the same headwinds buyers currently see . and if your area is likely to be hard - hit by layoffs or a potential economic recession , that will make qualified buyers even more scarce . 
 before you list your home , make sure you have a good understanding of how much it ’s worth , so you’ll know what kind of profit you stand to make and if it will be worth it . 
 next steps 
 if you think you ’re ready to start your home buying journey , it ’s important to keep saving as much as possible and working on your credit . a bigger down payment can save you thousands in mortgage principal and interest in the long run , and a higher credit score will help you snag a more competitive rate , which will also result in a more affordable monthly payment . 
 if you ’re ready to sell , pay attention to the prices homes in your area are asking — and ultimately selling for . note , too , the impression your home is likely to leave on potential buyers . if some spots could use a bit of sprucing up , now is the time . 
 whichever side of the transaction you ’re on , be sure to team up with an experienced real estate agent who can help you navigate your local market successfully . a knowledgeable agent can help sellers price and market their home competitively , and help buyers negotiate a good deal on a home that meets their needs . ask friends and family for recommendations and interview several candidates before settling on the right agent for you . 
 faqs 
 are home prices dropping or rising in the u . s . ? 
 while individual markets may see ebbs and flows , overall , prices in the u.s. are rising — and have been for some time . in march 2025 , existing - home prices rose year - over - year for the 21st consecutive month , according to data from the national association of realtors . 
 is the u.s. housing market going to crash ? 
 no . the u.s. housing market has cooled , but experts generally agree that it will not crash . this is largely due to the continued rise in home prices , minimal foreclosures and tight mortgage requirements .

housing market horizons : economic trends in real estate 
 06 / 29 / 2025 
 marcos vinicius 
 as we navigate the aftermath of a global pandemic and shifting economic tides , the real estate sector stands at a critical inflection point . from supply challenges and affordability pressures to emerging investment opportunities , the next five years promise both complexity and potential . 
 global housing market overview 
 the world is facing a global supply shortage of housing , with an estimated 6.5 million units needed in developed economies alone . this gap has fuelled an unprecedented affordability crisis , pushing more than 80 % of households toward renting . institutional investors , particularly in europe and asia , are expanding pipelines to close this void and emulate the u.s. model of large - scale multifamily projects . 
 rental demand surging as homeownership drifts out of reach . 
 multinational capital flowing into traditional apartment sectors . 
 single - family rentals poised to outperform apartment returns . 
 location - specific strategies driving tailored developments . 
 demographic trends — from aging populations to urban migration — are reshaping global demand . as cities densify and suburbs expand , investors and policymakers must align supply with evolving household structures . 
 the u.s. housing market : 2025 - 2029 
 in the united states , inventory levels have improved yet remain shy of a balanced marketplace . as of may 2025 , home inventory jumped 31 . 5 % year - over - year but still trails pre - pandemic figures by 14 % . newly listed homes climbed 7 . 2 % , and the median days on market have reverted to 51 days , near historical norms . 
 new homes for sale at 481 , 000 units — the highest since 2007 . 
 speculative builds at 385 , 000 units — the highest since 2008 . 
 pending sales down 2 . 5 % , signaling a transitional phase . 
 price appreciation is forecast at a modest 2 – 3 % annually through 2029 . the median list price in may 2025 held steady at $ 440 , 000 , while price cuts reached 19 . 1 % of listings — an indication of segmental oversupply and softening demand . 
 high home prices and mortgage rates have cemented an affordability gap that continues to widen . rental markets remain robust , with annual rent growth of 2 – 3 % expected . single - family rentals , in particular , are likely to lead future growth as households seek space and stability . 
 commercial and sectoral trends 
 the office sector has entered an up - cycle that is gaining momentum from 2024 onward . by late 2025 , premium downtown space is expected to tighten , supporting rent recovery . retail real estate hits its lowest vacancy in years , driven by suburban and sun belt demand . 
 industrial properties , fueled by e - commerce , are stabilizing leasing volumes at pre - pandemic levels , though legacy warehouses face higher vacancies . meanwhile , data centers are experiencing rapid expansion driven by ai and cloud services — power constraints are steering new builds toward nuclear and renewable energy solutions . 
 regional & demographic considerations 
 regional divergence defines the u.s. outlook . the northeast and midwest sustain price levels due to inventory constraints , while the south and west see varied growth — sun belt cities remain the hottest markets . globally , europe and asia race to scale institutional - grade multifamily supply , often learning from u.s. suburban and exurban models . 
 demographic shifts — such as millennial household formation , aging baby boomers , and remote work migration — are reshaping where and how people live . developers and policymakers must cater to dynamic household formation patterns , ensuring infrastructure and services align with emerging communities . 
 broader economic outlook and practical strategies 
 steady u.s. economic growth underpins real estate fundamentals , despite inflationary headwinds and political shifts . with 10-year treasury yields above 4 % , investors seek tangible returns in property . yet uncertainty over tariffs , work - from - home trends , and policy changes demands flexibility . 
 to thrive in this environment , stakeholders should adopt these practical approaches : 
 monitor local inventory and price movements to time market entry . 
 consider single - family rentals for portfolio diversification . 
 lock in favorable financing ahead of anticipated rate dips . 
 align new developments with migration and demographic data . 
 by focusing on long - term market trajectories and agile decision - making , buyers , renters , and investors can position themselves for success over the 2025 – 2029 horizon . 
 the coming half - decade will test the resilience and creativity of all market participants . by embracing data - driven insights , prioritizing affordability , and investing in sustainable growth , the real estate industry can pave the way for more equitable and prosperous communities worldwide . 
 as horizons broaden , so do opportunities . whether you are a first - time buyer navigating mortgage rates , an investor diversifying across sectors , or a policymaker shaping urban policy , the keys to success lie in foresight , flexibility , and a steadfast commitment to meeting the evolving needs of society .
