2.title: 【徹底分析】「フォーチュン500」未掲載のPalantirがグローバル企業の頂点に立った驚異の成長戦略 | Australia
2.content:
【 徹底 分析 】 「 フォーチュン 500 」 未 掲載 の palantir が グローバル 企業 の 頂点 に 立っ た 驚異 の 成長 戦略 
 author : 
 f0xtr0t published : 2025 - 08 - 08 20 : 06 : 02 
 palantir と は どの よう な 企業 か ？ 
 フォーチュン 500 未 掲載 企業 が グローバル プレイヤー に なった 理由 
 財務 パフォーマンス から 見る 成長 軌道 
 専門家 は palantir の 成長 持続 性 を どう 見 ている か ？ 
 palantir が 示す 「 新しい テック 企業 の 形 」 
 palantir に関するよくある質問 
 データ 分析 を 武器 にした 「 影 の テック ジャイアント 」 palantir technologies が 、 ここ 数 年 で 見せ た 急 成長 は 業界 の 常識 を 覆す もの だ 。 フォーチュン 500 には 未 掲載 ながら 、 政府 契約 と 民間 企業 向け プラット フォーム の 両輪 で 収益 を 拡大 し 、 2025 年 現在 では 時価 総額 で 多く の 老舗 企業 を 凌駕 し ている 。 本 記事 では 、 その 独自 ビジネス モデル と 競争 優位 性 の 核心 を 、 財務 データ と 市場 動向 を 交え て 多角的 に 分析 する 。 
 palantir と は どの よう な 企業 か ？ 
 2003 年 に ピーター ・ ティール ら によって 設立 された palantir は 、 当初 cia 向け の データ 分析 ソフトウェア 開発 から スタート し た 。 創業 時 の 出資 元 が paypal マフィア と 呼ば れる シリコン バレー の エリート 集団 だっ た こと も あり 、 その 出自 から し て 「 普通 の テック 企業 」 と は 一線 を 画し て い た 。 私 が 初めて palantir の デモ を 見 た 時 、 その 可視化 技術 の 精度 には 正直 鳥肌 が 立っ た 覚え が ある 。 
 同社 の コア 製品 で ある gotham プラット フォーム は 、 テロ 対策 や サイバー セキュリティ 分野 で 米国 政府 機関 から 絶大 な 信頼 を 得 て おり 、 2021 年度 の 政府 契約 額 だけで 7 億 3000 万 ドル に 達し ている （ 出典 ： us as pending . gov ） 。 
 フォーチュン 500 未 掲載 企業 が グローバル プレイヤー に なった 理由 
 一般的 に フォーチュン 500 入り は 企業 の 規模 を 示す 重要 な 指標 と さ れる が 、 palantir の 場合 この リスト に 掲載 されて い ない こと が 逆 に 興味深 い 。 という の も 、 同社 の ビジネス モデル は 伝統 的 な 収益 構造 と は 根本 的 に 異なる からだ 。 2025 年 第 2 四半期 時点 で 、 palantir の 時価 総額 は 約 450 億 ドル （ 出典 ： trading vie w ） に 達し て おり 、 これ は フォーチュン 500 企業 の 多く を 上回る 水準 だ 。 
 その 成功 要因 を 分析 する と 、 以下 の 3 つの 競争 優位 性 が 浮かび上がる ： 
 政府 機関 向け 高 単価 ソリューション の 独占 的 シェア 
 民間 企業向け foundry プラットフォーム の 急 成長 
 ai アルゴリズム と 人間 の 分析 を 融合 し た 独自 アプローチ 
 財務 パフォーマンス から 見る 成長 軌道 
 palantir の 2025 年 第 1 四半期 決算 は 、 市場 予想 を 大幅 に 上回る 内容 だっ た 。 収益 は 前年 比 34 % 増 の 6 億 2800 万 ドル 、 営業 利益 率 は ついに 15 % の 大台 を 突破 し た 。 特に 注目 す べき は 民間 部門 の 成長 で 、 契約 件数 が 四半期 ベース で 40 % 増加 し ている （ 出典 ： palantir ir レポート ） 。 
 指標 2023 年度 2024 年度 2025 年 q 2 
 総 収益 19 億 ドル 22 億 ドル 6 . 28 億 ドル 
 営業利益率 5 % 11 % 15 % 
 政府 契約 比率 56 % 49 % 45 % 
 専門家 は palantir の 成長 持続 性 を どう 見 ている か ？ 
 btc c の シシニア アナリスト 、 ジェームズ ・ ウィルソン 氏 は 「 palantir の 真 の 強み は 、 10 年 以上 にわたる 実 運用 データ の 蓄積 にある 」 と 指摘 する 。 確か に 、 同社 の ai モデル が 他社 と 一線 を 画す の は 、 実際 の テロ 対策 や 金融 犯罪 調査 で 鍛え られ た アルゴリズム にあると 言える だろ う 。 
 一方 で 、 倫理 的 懸念 を 指摘 する 声 も ある 。 プライバシー 擁護 団体 e pi c は 2024 年 、 palantir の 移民 当局 向け システム 使用 に関して 抗議 活動 を 展開 し た 。 こうした 課題 を 乗り越え られる か が 、 今後 の 持続 的 成長 の 鍵 と なる だろ う 。 
 palantir が 示す 「 新しい テック 企業 の 形 」 
 従来 の gafa 型 モデル と は 異なり 、 palantir は 「 b 2 g 」 （ 企業 to 政府 ） という 特殊 な 分野 で 成功 を 収め た 稀有 な 例 だ 。 個人的 な 見解 だ が 、 彼ら の 成長 ストーリー は 、 サブ スクリプションモデル 全盛 の 現代 において 、 高 単価 な エンタープライズ ソリューション 市場 の 可能性 を 改めて 示し た と 言える 。 
 2025 年 現在 、 同社 は 医療 データ 分析 や 気候 変動 対策 といった 新 分野 に も 積極的 に 進出 し ている 。 今後 の 展開 次第 では 、 フォーチュン 500 どころか 、 テック 業界 の 勢力 図 そのもの を 塗り替える 可能性 を 秘め ている だろ う 。 
 palantir に関するよくある質問 
 palantir が フォーチュン 500 に 掲載 されて いない 理由 は ？ 
 フォーチュン 500 は 主 に 売上高 に 基づい て 企業 を ランク 付け し て おり 、 palantir の 場合 、 収益 規模 が まだ リスト の 基準 に 達し て い ない ため です 。 ただし 時価 総額 では 多く の 掲載 企業 を 上回っ て います 。 
 palantir の 主 な 競合 企業 は どこ ですか ？ 
 政府 向け データ分析 分 野 では caci インターナショナル 、 民間 企業向け では s now flake や splunk など が 主要 競合 として 挙げ られ ます 。 ただし palantir の 技術 スタック は 独自 性 が 高く 、 完全 に 代替 可能 な 競合 は 存在 し ない という 見方 も あり ます 。 
 個人 投資家 にとって palantir 株 は 魅力 的 ですか ？ 
 btc c アナリスト チーム に よれ ば 、 palantir 株 は 高い 成長 可能性 を 持つ 一方 、 バ リュ エーション 水準 や 政府 依存度 など の リスク 要因 も 考慮 する 必要 があります 。 投資 判断 の 前 には 必ず 独自 の 調査 を 行って ください 。

3.title: 11/4に決算発表があったPalantir$PLTR の内容についてのまとめ|米株投資家 米国の投資家発言まとめ
3.content:
11 / 4 に 決算 発表 が あっ た palantir $ pltr の 内容 について の まとめ 
 米 株 投資家 米国 の 投資家 発言 まとめ 
 2024 年 11 月 5 日 07 : 23 
 1. 売上 ・ 利益 構造 の 詳細 
 パ ランティア は 第 3 四半期 において 、 売上高 が 前年 同期 比 約 19 % 増 の 5 億 6000 万 ドル に 達し まし た 。 この 成長 は 政府 向け 事業 と 商業 向け 事業 の 両方 の 堅調 な 伸び に 支え られ て います 。 売上 の 成長率 は 前年 より 若干 鈍化 し ている ものの 、 安定的 な 成長 が 続い て おり 、 市場 の 期待 を 上回る 結果 を 達成 し まし た 。 
 特に 政府 部門 で の 売上 は 米 国防総省 、 国土 安全 保障 省 など の 大 規模 な 契約 が 牽引 し て おり 、 パ ランティア の セキュリティ 関連 技術 に対する 需要 が 引き続き 高い こと が 窺え ます 。 米国 政府 と の 契約 は 安定 収入 の 柱 で あり 、 契約 の 拡張 や 新規 プロジェクト の 獲得 が 続く こと で 、 今後 も 持続 的 な 売上 成長 が 期待 されます 。 
 商業 部門 について は 、 米国 国内 の 顧客 獲得 数 が 増加 し て おり 、 既存 顧客 の 契約 更新 や 新規 案件 の 増加 も 顕著 です 。 特に 医療 、 製造 、 小売 など 幅広い 業種 で の 導入 が 進んで おり 、 データ 活用 の ニーズ が 商業 部門 の 成長 を 支え て います 。 
 利益 面 では 、 営業 利益 率 が 前年 同期 よりも 改善 し て おり 、 gaap ベース で の 収益性 の 向上 が 見 られ ます 。 非 gaap ベース の 調整 後 eps も 市場 予測 を 上回る 結果 と なり 、 パ ランティア が 収益性 向上 の ため の 経費 管理 に 成功 し ている こと が 示さ れ て います 。 
 2. 各 プロダクト の 成長 と ai へ の 投資 
 パ ランティア の 製品 ポート フォリオ の 中核 を 担う の が 、 found ry 、 apollo 、 gotham の 3 つの 主要 プラット フォーム です 。 これら は 、 それぞれ 商業 顧客 、 政府 機関 向け の データ 解析 や 管理 の ニーズ に 応える 製品 で 、 顧客 企業 が 大量 の データ を 効果 的 に 分析 ・ 利用 できる よう に する ため の 技術 基盤 を 提供 してい ます 。 
 • foundry : 商業 部 門 で の データ 活用 ニーズ に 特 化 した プラットフォーム で 、 各 業界 で の データ 統合 、 ai 活用 に 利用 されて い ます 。 特に ai の 統合 プラットフォーム として の foundry for ai が 注目 されて おり 、 企業 が 自社 の データ を 解析 する 際 の 基盤 を 簡素 化 する 役割 を 担い ます 。 found ry for ai は 、 企業 が 生成 ai や 機械 学習 モデル を 活用 しやすい 形 で 提供 さ れ 、 企業 の ai 戦略 を サポート する 存在 として 高い 評価 を 受けて います 。 
 • apollo : クラウド と エッジ の 双方 で 展開 できる ソフトウェア デリバリー の 自動 化 ツール で 、 アップデート 管理 や 導入 作業 を 効率 化し ます 。 apollo により 、 パ ランティア の ソフトウェア が 様々 な 環境 下 で 安定 し て 稼働 できる こと が 保証 さ れ 、 顧客 企業 は システム の 継続 的 な 改善 を 容易 に 行う こと が でき ます 。 
 • gotham : 米国 政府 向け に 特 化し た データ 解析 プラット フォーム で 、 安全 保障 、 テロ 対策 など の 分野 で 使わ れ て います 。 got ham は リアルタイム で 大量 の データ を 解析 し 、 政府 機関 の 意思 決定 を 支援 する 重要 な 役割 を 果たして おり 、 セキュリティ 面 で の 技術 的 な 信頼性 が 評価 されて います 。 
 特に ai （ 人工知能 ） 技術 へ の 投資 が 増加 し て おり 、 foundry for ai が 同社 の ai 戦略 の 中核 を 成す 存在 と なって います 。 パ ランティア は ai を通じて 顧客 企業 が 保有 する データ から 洞察 を 得る 支援 を 行う だけで なく 、 ai 活用 に対する 顧客 企業 の 抵抗 を 軽減 し 、 導入 プロセス を 効率 化 する 役割 を 担っ て います 。 将来 的 には 生成 ai 分野 で の 技術 革新 に も 積極的 に 取り組み 、 新た な 収益 源 の 確立 を 目指し て います 。 
 3. 第 4 四半期 と 今後 の 成長 戦略 
 パ ランティア は 、 今後 の 成長 戦略 として ai 分野 へ の さら なる 投資 を 強調 してい ます 。 第 4 四半期 に 向け て 、 売上 が 引き続き 増加 する と 見込ま れ て おり 、 特に ai 分野 で の 市場 機会 が 成長 を 支える と 考え られ て います 。 found ry for ai の 拡張 により 、 商業 部門 で の さらなる 導入 拡大 が 期待 されて おり 、 また 政府 部門 でも ai を 活用 し た 新しい ソリューション 提供 が 予定 されて います 。 
 ai 市場 は 今後 数 年 で 急 成長 が 見込ま れ て おり 、 パ ランティア は この 分野 で の 競争力 を 高める こと で 、 顧客 から の ニーズ に 迅速 に 対応 できる 体制 を 整える ことを 目指し て います 。 特に 、 政府 部門 と 商業 部門 の 双方 で の データ 解析 や ai 活用 の ニーズ は 高まっ て おり 、 パ ランティア の 強み で ある データ 解析 技術 と ai の 組み合わせ は 、 今後 の 成長 を 加速 させる と 期待 されて います 。 
 4. 財務 健全性 と 投資家 へ の アピール 
 パ ランティア は 収益性 改善 に 加え て 、 健全 な 財務 体制 を 維持 し ている ことを 強調 してい ます 。 同社 の バランス シート は 強 固 で 、 豊富 な キャッシュ リザーブ を 有し ている ため 、 積極的 な r & d （ 研究 開発 ） や m & a （ 合併 ・ 買収 ） など 、 今後 の 成長 に 向け た 投資 も 可能 です 。 これ により 、 財務 的 な リスク を 最小限 に 抑え つつ 、 競争力 を 高める ため の 戦略的 な 動き が と れる 状況 に あり ます 。 
 投資家 から の 視点 では 、 同社 が 収益 性 と 成長 性 を 両立 させ ている 点 が 評価 されて おり 、 ai 分野 における 先進 的 な ポジション や 、 安定 し た 政府 契約 に 基づく 収益 基盤 が 注目 されて います 。 また 、 ai 技術 の 展開 に 伴い 、 今後 の 収益 の 成長 が 加速 する 可能性 が ある 点 も 投資家 にとって は 魅力 的 な 要素 です 。 
 5. 株価 と 市場 の 反応 
 決算 発表 後 、 パ ランティア の 株価 は 時間 外 取引 で 一時的 に 急上昇 し まし た 。 これ は 予想 を 上回る 売上 と 利益 、 そして ai 技術 へ の 投資 が 今後 の 成長 を 支える と の 期待 感 による もの です 。 市場 では ai 技術 へ の 積極 投資 が 収益性 の 向上 に 結びつく と の 見方 が 強まっ て おり 、 パ ランティア は 次世代 の 技術 企業 として の ポジション を 確立 し つつ あり ます 。 
 ただし 、 株価 は これ まで の 急激 な 上昇 から 調整 局面 に 入り つつ ある とも 言え ます 。 パ ランティア が ai 市場 で の シェア を 拡大 できる か 、 また 商業 部門 と 政府 部門 の 売上 が バランス よく 成長 する か が 、 今後 の 株価 に 大きな 影響 を 与える でしょ う 。 
 6. まとめ と 展望 
 パ ランティア の 第 3 四半期 決算 は 、 売上 と 利益 の 双方 で 市場 予想 を 上回り 、 特に ai 技術 へ の 積極的 な 投資 が 将来 の 成長 を 支える と 期待 されて います 。 商業 部門 と 政府 部門 の 双方 で 顧客 基盤 の 拡大 が 進んで おり 、 ai ソリューション へ の 需要 が 高まり 続け て います 。 found ry for ai を 始め と する 製品 の 成長 が パ ランティア の 競争力 を さらに 強化 する 一方 で 、 今後 の 収益性 の 改善 も 視野 に 入れ て います 。 
 将来 的 には 、 ai と データ 解析 が 一体 と なった ソリューション 提供 が 、 商業 部門 の 成長 と 政府 部門 の 安定 収益 に 貢献 する こと が 期待 されて います 。

4.title: Palantirの「軍・政府から民間」への拡張戦略【時系列まとめ】|さんろく
4.content:
palantir の 「 軍 ・ 政府 から 民間 」 へ の 拡張 戦略 【 時系列 まとめ 】 
 さん ろく 
 2025 年 5 月 7 日 14:42 
 ✅ 【 2003 年 〜 2015 年 】 ： 政府 特 化 フェーズ （ “ 隠れ cia ” 時代 ） 
 ▶ 主 な 事業 領域 
 米軍 （ dod ） 、 cia 、 nsa 、 fbi など へ の テロ 対策 ・ 防 諜 ・ 戦場 分析 。 
 情報 の 断片 を 統合 し て 「 テロ を 未然 に 防ぐ 」 ため の got ham が 主力 。 
 ▶ 戦略 的 意図 
 最も 緊 急性 が 高く 、 予算 が 潤沢 な 「 国家 安全 保障 」 から 着手 。 
 機密 性 ・ 特殊性 の 高さ ゆえ 、 商用 展開 は 想定 されて い なかっ た 。 
 🎯 palantir は 「 国家 の 諜報 機関 の ため の ソフト 」 として 誕生 。 完全 な gov tech 専 業 。 
 ✅ 【 2016 年 〜 2019 年 】 ： 民間 展開 の 布石 （ foundry の 誕生 ） 
 ▶ 主 な 動き 
 米国 大手 金融 機関 ・ 航空機 メーカー （ boeing ・ air bus ） など へ の poc 提供 （ 試験 導入 ） 。 
 ヘルスケア 、 エネルギー 、 製造業 向け の データ 基盤 ソフト 「 foundry 」 を 開発 。 
 ▶ 戦略 的 意図 
 「 民間 でも 複雑 な サプライチェーン や センサー データ が 扱えれば 勝てる 」 
 → 軍事 インフラ で 培っ た 高度 な 統合 技術 を 商業 に 転用 。 
 汎用性 の ある データ 可視化 エンジン ＋ 業務 プロセス の 再 構築 が 核 。 
 ▶ 実績 
 air bus における 整備 スケジュール 最適化 。 
 bp （ 石油 ） における 設備 稼働率 と 原油 パイプライン の 監視 強化 。 
 🏗 ️ 「 戦争 の 複雑性 」 は 「 グローバル ビジネス の 複雑性 」 に 似 て い た 。 
 ✅ 【 2020 年 〜 2021 年 】 ： covid - 19 と 商用 転換 の 加速 
 ▶ 主 な 動き 
 パンデミック 下 で foundry を 米 ・ 英 の 医療 システム に 提供 （ 例 ： 米 hhs 、 英 nhs ） 。 
 ワクチン 配布 の 最適化 、 病床 管理 、 物流 の デジタル ツイン 化 に 寄与 。 
 ▶ 戦略 的 意図 
 政府 ・ 準 公的 機関 と 民間 医療 機関 の * * “ 橋渡し ” 分野 で の 成功 * * により 、 「 商用 実績 」 を 獲得 。 
 ipo （ 2020 年 9 月 ） の タイミング と 重なり 、 民間 市場 へ の アピール が 加速 。 
 ▶ 実績 
 米国 の 複数 州 における 医療 機関 の データ 統合 支援 。 
 製薬 企業向け ： 創 薬 シミュレーション データ 管理 に foundry 導入 。 
 💊 公共 インフラ と 企業 活動 の 境界線 が 曖昧 に なる 中 、 palantir は “ 両面 対応 os ” と なる 。 
 ✅ 【 2022 年 〜 2023 年 】 ： 米国 企業 向け 拡大 と 欧州 進出 
 ▶ 主 な 動き 
 米 大手 食品 ・ 飲料 ・ 製造業 （ hyundai 、 kws 、 ferrari な ど ） へ の 導入 が 進行 。 
 特に 製造業 の サプライチェーン 管理 ・ 予測 保守 ・ 原材料 価格 分析 など で 成果 。 
 欧州 では 「 エネルギー 価格 高騰 」 対応 として foundry 導入 が 急増 。 
 ▶ 戦略 的 意図 
 “ defense - grade software ” を ノーコード 化 ・ ux 強化 し て 企業 現場 に 対応 。 
 導入 障壁 （ 学習 コスト ・ ライセンス 費 ） を 下げ 、 sa as 化 準備 を 進行 。 
 ▶ 実績 
 hyundai の 工場 iot データ分析 に foundry 導入 。 
 ferrari の ev 設計 シミュレーション へ の 活用 。 
 医薬 企業 が 臨床 試験 データ を 統合 ・ 予測 分析 。 
 🧱 palantir の コア は 軍事 レベル の 堅牢性 。 だからこそ 、 金融 や 製造業 で 通用 し た 。 
 ✅ 【 2023 年 〜 現在 】 ： aip （ ai platform ） による 商用 シフト の 決定 打 
 ▶ 主 な 動き 
 生成 ai （ llm ） を 業務 アプリ に 埋め込ん だ 新 基盤 「 aip 」 提供 開始 。 
 製造業 、 金融 、 保険 、 小売業 界 で 業務 命令 の ai 化 ・ 自動化 が 拡大 。 
 ▶ 戦略 的 意図 
 openai や anthropic など と は 異なり 、 「 機密 × ai 」 の ドメイン で 差別化 。 
 aip は 「 企業 内 gpt 」 ＋ 「 業務 オペレーション 統合 」 の ハイブリッド 構造 。 
 一般的 な ai ベンチャー では 扱え ない 政府 ・ 金融 ・ 軍事 並み の 複雑 性 と セキュリティ に 対応 。 
 ▶ 実績 
 j.d. power （ 自動車 リサーチ ） における 顧客 データ 分析 と パーソナ ライズ 。 
 米 大手 製造業 における 故障 予測 と 意思 決定 支援 ai 。 
 🤖 palantir は 「 企業 gpt を 超え た 、 “ 軍事 レベル の コパイロット ” 」 を 目指し ている 。 
 総括 ： 政府 で 育ち 、 民間 に “ 降り て き た ” 異端 の エンタープライズ os 
 palantir とは 、 「 最 も 遅れ て きた が 、 最 も 頼 り に なる エンタープライズ saas 」 である 。

 company overview 
 palantir technologies is a leading american software company specializing in big data analytics and ai - powered decision intelligence platforms . founded to help intelligence agencies detect terrorist threats while preserving civil liberties , palantir has evolved into a global enterprise serving defense , intelligence , law enforcement , and commercial clients across 50 + industries . its platforms , gotham , foundry , apollo , and aip ( artificial intelligence platform ) , integrate vast , disparate datasets into unified , operationally actionable systems , enabling real - time insights , predictive analytics , and autonomous ai agent orchestration .

6.title: Will a New Microsoft Partnership Help Launch Palantir's Stock to the Moon? | Nasdaq
6.content:

 pltr - 0 . 31 % 
 will a new microsoft partnership help launch palantir 's stock to the moon ? 
 august 17 , 2024 — 01 : 17 pm edt 
 written by geoffrey seiler for the motley fool - > 
 days after reporting strong second - quarter results , palantir technologies ( nyse : pltr ) gave investors even more good news when it announced an expanded partnership with microsoft ( nasdaq : msft ) . the aim is to sell analytic and artificial - intelligence ( ai ) services to various defense and intelligence agencies within the federal government . 
 palantir built its reputation helping u.s. government intelligence agencies track and fight terrorism through its data gathering and analytics platform , but the government has actually become one of the weak spots for the company over the past couple of years . let 's look at how this deal could change that . 
 looking to boost federal government sales 
 the u.s. government has long been palantir 's largest customer , although its growth has become a weak spot for the company . total government revenue growth , including foreign governments , slowed to 19 % in 2022 and only 14 % in 2023. 
 it has seen a bit of a rebound this year , with total government revenue growth of 23 % year over year to $ 371 million in the second quarter and u.s. government growth of 24 % to $ 278 million . 
 however , that still trailed its faster - growing commercial segment , which saw a year - over - year increase of 33 % to $ 307 million in the quarter . commercial revenue in the u . s . , in particular , grew even faster at 55 % to $ 159 million . 
 this partnership with microsoft will look to kick start growth in its u.s. government segment . palantir 's entire suite of products will be now be able to be deployed using microsoft 's government cloud , including microsoft azure government , azure government secret , and azure top secret cloud . the partnership will also use azure 's openai service and integrate its large language models , including gpt - 4 , into palantir 's foundry software and its artificial intelligence platform ( aip ) . 
 one of the big goals of the partnership will be to help speed up deployments , especially with aip . in combination with microsoft , the company will run boot camps to let the defense and intelligence community test the technology . 
 palantir has been very successful in driving new customer acquisitions with its boot camps in the commercial sector , and it will look to take that to the federal sector as well . these workshops provide training and demonstrate how aip can be applied to mission - critical operations and other potential uses . 
 one downside to palantir 's government business is that it can be contract work for specific projects . if the company can begin integrating aip into more government workloads , it can help create a longer - lasting , more reliably recurring revenue stream . providing ai services to various government defense and intelligence agencies is a huge opportunity for the company , and the microsoft partnership should make getting approvals easier . 
 image source : getty images . 
 is the stock a buy ? 
 palantir has proved the strength of its technology , but the one thing that keeps many investors cautious is its valuation . the stock trades at a forward price - to - sales ratio ( p / s ) of about 20 times based on 2025 analyst estimates . 
 pltr ps ratio ( forward 1 y ) ; data by ycharts . 
 for a company growing revenue by under 30 % , that is quite an expensive multiple . to justify that , it would need to accelerate it beyond 30 % . palantir has begun to see a rebound in its u.s. government business , and this new partnership could reinvigorate that even more . but based on its current valuation , it appears the market is already pricing that happening into the stock . 
 i think palantir has a good long - term opportunity , but given its valuation , i would rather be a buyer on a pullback . even the best tech companies go through periods when their stock prices fall , and i 'd prefer to be patient and not chase the shares at these valuations .

 はじめに 
 palantir technologies （ パ ランティア ） は 、 政府 機関 ・ 大企業 向け に データ 統合 ・ 分析 ソフトウェア を 提供 する 企業 です 。 政府 向け 「 gotham 」 、 商業 向け 「 found ry 」 、 そして ai 統合 の 中核 「 aip （ artificial intelligence platform ） 」 を 軸 に 、 データ 主導 の 意思 決定 と オペレーション 最適化 を 支援 します 。 
 本 記事 は 、 主 に fy 2019 ～ fy 2024 の 公式 開示 に 基づく 財務 ・ kpi の 整理 と 、 aip を 中心 と し た 事業 戦略 、 競争 環境 、 2025 年 の 注目 ポイント を 投資家 視点 で 解説 します 。 
 【 免責 ・ 出典 】 
 数値 は palantir の 年次 報告書 （ form 10 - k ） 、 四半期 報告書 （ form 10 - q ） 、 決算 リリース 等 の 公式 ir に 基づき 作成 。 fy 2024 は 2024 年 12 月 期 実績 です 。

8.title: Palantirs Rise in Global Government & Defence
8.content:
palanti rs rise in global government & defence 
 scaling sovereign - class data platforms across governments , defence agencies , and coalitions 
 introduction 
 few technology firms have so thoroughly embedded themselves into the operational fabric of governments and defence as palantir technologies . born in the post-9/11 era with secretive intelligence roots , palantir has redirected its trajectory toward becoming a sovereign - class software enabler across five eyes , nato , eu states and beyond . 
 this case study examines how palantir scaled , the institutional strategy underpinning its growth , deployment across defence and civil government , and lessons for organisations operating in dual - use , high - assurance environments . 
 1. origins , founding vision & strategic positioning 
 palantir was founded in 2003 , backed by early investments from in - q - tel and venture capital aligned with u.s. intelligence interests . its early mission was to support counterterrorism by fusing data and surfacing insights . over time , it evolved from niche research tool to an enterprise - grade data platform stack . 
 key strategic differentiators from early days : 
 data abstraction and ontology - first modeling — palantir ’s emphasis on rigorous data modeling ( ontologies , entity relationships ) allowed it to connect messy government data silos . 
 rapid deployment mindset — palantir deploys with forward - deployed engineers ( fdes ) inside customers , enabling high - trust integration at scale . 
 dual - use trajectory — initially defence / intel only , palantir expanded into civilian domains ( health , logistics , supply chain ) to broaden its addressable market . 
 its architecture supports classified and unclassified domains , allowing developers to build pipelines , dashboards , decision support , and ai / ml layers atop a flexible substrate . 
 2. anchoring defence & government as primary customers 
 palantir ’s strategy hinged on governments as anchor clients . once trusted in defence or intelligence , revenue expansion into commercial and civil sectors becomes easier . 
 2.1 u.s. department of defense & intelligence 
 jadc2 / abms ( joint all - domain command & control / advanced battle management system ) : palantir is positioning its platform as a nerve center for sensor and effects orchestration across air , land , sea , space , and cyber . 
 army vantage contract : reports indicate contracts in the hundreds of millions of dollars to deliver data fusion , analytics , and operational dashboards . 
 special operations command and intelligence agencies rely on palantir for counterterrorism , targeting , and data fusion . 
 by embedding at the “ sensor - to - shooter ” level , palantir ensures persistent relevance to kinetic operations . analysts suggest palantir ’s ai - enabled systems dominate defence pipeline projections worth over $ 1 b in contracts . a invest + 1 
 2.2 united kingdom & five eyes allies 
 palantir sells “ sovereign versions ” or partner - integrated derivatives in uk , canada , australia , and new zealand operations . in the uk , palantir has participated in mod digital transformation projects , using the platform to unify intelligence , logistics , and ops data silos . 
 within the uk , there has been discussion of a “ sovereign foundry ” to reduce dependence on foreign software while retaining palantir - like capability . klover 
 2.3 nato , eu , and coalition deployment 
 at an alliance level , palantir ’s platform is used for data - sharing , cross - border crisis monitoring , covid response , migrant flow analytics , and joint exercises . by serving as a neutral fabric , palantir enables interoperability across national systems . 
 governments also use it to respond to crises ( e . g . natural disasters , pandemics ) — for example , deploying dashboards that fuse hospital data , logistics , and supply chain flows . 
 3. scaling strategy & business model 
 palantir ’s scaling has followed a playbook worth dissecting . 
 3.1 “ operational first , enterprise next ” 
 rather than building a massive selling - machine , palantir invests heavily in operational pilot deployments . that is : embed a solution with a small team on the frontline or analytic cell , deliver value rapidly , then scale outward . that progression builds trust , buy - in , and anchors institutional adoption . 
 3.2 forward - deployed engineers ( fdes ) 
 palantir ’s fdes are embedded inside customer environments , working hand - in - glove with operator teams . this model breaks down trust barriers , accelerates iteration , and ensures the product evolves with real requirements . the fde model is costly , but it builds stickiness and domain alignment . 
 3.3 ecosystem partnerships & integrators 
 palantir encourages external integrators , defense primes , systems integrators , smes ( like aic - scale integrators ) to build modules , ontologies , and domain logic that run on top of the palantir “ core . ” this creates a two - sided marketplace : palantir handles the substrate ; partners build domain stack . 
 this is critical because no one organization can deeply understand every warfighting domain or classified environment ; an ecosystem helps scale domain talent . 
 3.4 data sovereignty , partitioning & trust zones 
 palantir invests in data architecture that partitions by classification , role , and trust . sovereign deployments require that no external infrastructure touches national secrets . palantir ’s customer architecture often includes isolated enclaves , air - gapped nodes , data sharding , and cross - domain guards . 
 3.5 commercial pull & civil crossover 
 once palantir is installed in a government environment , it can offer adjacent services : logistics analytics , disaster response , public health , supply chain optimization . these civil use - cases fund further product capabilities , which in turn feed defence demand . 
 4. successes , risks & critiques 
 4.1 success stories 
 ukraine conflict : palantir has been widely cited in media as operationally embedded in ukraine , helping fuse battlefield feeds , drone and satellite imagery , and targeting analytics into coherent decision pipelines . 
 revenue & valuation : palantir ’s 2025 surge has caught investor attention ; recent analysis shows institutional demand driving share price . seeking alpha + 2 the street + 2 
 long - term contracts : it has won multi - year , high - value defense contracts that anchor its revenue runway . 
 4.2 risks , criticism & limitations 
 vendor lock - in & dependency : governments may fear that deep reliance on palantir prohibits agility or competitive replacement . 
 sovereignty concerns : france , germany , and others have pushed for their own architectures or constrained use of u.s. platforms . 
 escalating cost base : the fde model is expensive ; scaling without ballooning costs is non - trivial . 
 transparency & trust : closed - source or opaque model layers risk auditability and accountability in defence settings . 
 political and regulatory exposure : as palantir grows , scrutiny arises from data privacy , surveillance , and ethical objections . 
 5. lessons for defense & government clients 
 anchor early via trusted use - case , not enterprise rollouts — begin with high - value pilot operations ( e . g . intel fusion , command center ) before scaling wide . 
 embed domain engineers ( analogous to fdes ) to avoid the “ black box vendor ” problem . 
 build partner ecosystems — local integrators , smes , ontologists to customize domain logic . 
 ensure sovereignty & air - gap capability — design the infrastructure so that no external access is needed for critical systems . 
 design for auditability and model explainability to satisfy legal / regulatory oversight . 
 evolve gradually — expand from defence into civil and dual - use analytics when legitimacy and trust are established . 
 prepare for strategic pushback — rivals may seek to limit dependence on large u.s. ai firms ; plan alternate paths or local clones . 
 6. conclusion 
 palantir ’s journey demonstrates how a software company can evolve from niche intelligence tools to a backbone of global government and defence architectures . the strategic playbook of embedding trusted pilots , investing in forward - deployed engineering , and building a partner ecosystem is instructive . however , the future will test palantir ’s ability to balance sovereignty , cost , trust , and competition , especially as governments increasingly demand localised or autonomous alternatives . 
 for any organisation seeking to operate in defense - intelligence domains at scale , the palantir case offers both inspiration and caution — you must deliver utility , trust , and institutional alignment before you can scale .

9.title: Palantir株の今後の展望|成長性・リスクは?
9.content:
palantir 株 の 今後 の 展望 ｜ 成長 性 ・ リスク は ？ 
 直近 の 決算 ハイライト 
 パ ランティア ・ テクノロジーズ の 2025 年 12 月 期 第 1 四半期 は 、 収益 が 8 . 84 億 ドル と 前年 同期 比 39 . 4 % 増加 し 、 会社 予測 の 上限 を 上回る 結果 と なりました 。 営業 収益 も 1 . 76 億 ドル と 前年 の 2 . 17 倍 に 達し て います 。 
 部門 別 では 、 政府 関連 の 売上 が 4 . 87 億 ドル と 45 . 4 % 増加 。 特に 米国 政府 向け は 3 . 73 億 ドル と なり 、 米軍 へ の 人工 知能 搭載 戦術 情報 車両 「 titan 」 の 納入 が 開始 されました 。 この 製品 は 衛星 や 航空機 から の データ を 統合 し 、 即座 に 作戦 判断 できる 機能 を 持っ て います 。 政府 関連 の 取引 先 数 も 140 から 147 へ と 拡大 し まし た 。 
 民間 企業向け ビジネス も 3 . 97 億 ドル と 32 . 8 % 増加 し 、 特に 米 国内 では 70 % という 著 しい 伸び を 記録 し てい ます 。 取引先 数 は 372 から 397 社 へ と 増え 、 米 国内 では 214 から 255 社 に 拡大 しま した 。 
 この よう な 売上 増加 により 、 営業 利益 率 は 前年 同期 の 12 . 8 % から 大幅 に 改善 し 、 過去 最高 を 記録 し まし た 。 前期 に 計上 し た 従業員 向け 特別 報酬 の 影響 を 除い て も 、 収益性 は 大きく 向上 してい ます 。 
 出典 ： 楽天証券 トク シル 
 ai 需要 と の 関連 
 パ ランティア の 株価 は 、 人工 知能 技術 へ の 注目 度 の 高まり と 密接 に 関連 し て 推移 してい ます 。 北 大西洋 条約 機構 （ nato ） と の 大 規模 な 軍事 システム 契約 締結 は 、 防衛 分野 における 先端 技術 の 需要 拡大 を 象徴 する 出来事 として 市場 から 高く 評価 されて います 。 
 米 国内 の 企業 向け 売上 が 70 % 以上 も 増加 したこと は 、 民間 部門 でも 同社 の 技術 力 が 認め られ ている 証拠 です 。 特に 「 titan 」 と 呼ば れる 最新 情報 収集 車両 の 軍 へ の 引き渡し 開始 は 、 実用 段階 に 入っ た 技術 革新 として 投資家 の 関心 を 集め て います 。 
 専門家 たち は 同社 の 成長 性 を 、 先進 的 な 技術 基盤 と 着実 に 広がる 顧客 網 に 基づく 持続 可能 な ビジネス モデル として 評価 してい ます 。 将来 的 な 収益 増加 が 見込ま れる こと から 、 成長 志向 の 投資家 から 強い 支持 を 得 ている の です 。 
 市場 アナリスト の 間 では 、 パ ランティア の 株価 変動 は 人工 知能 産業 全体 の 動向 と 強く 結びついて いる と 考え られ て おり 、 同社 は 先端 技術 投資 の 指標 的 な 存在 と なって います 。 
 出典 ： 楽天証券 トク シル 
 潜在 的 な リスク や 注意点 
 パ ランティア 株 へ の 投資 を 検討 する 際 には 、 いくつ か の 重要 な 懸念 点 に 注意 する 必要 があります 。 まず 、 同社 の 株価 収益 率 は 約 150 倍 という 極めて 高い 水準 に あり 、 将来 の 成長 性 が すでに 現在 の 価格 に 反映 されて います 。 この ため 、 好調 な 業績 を 発表 し て も 株価 上昇 が 限定 的 で ある 一方 、 予想 を 下回れば 大幅 な 下落 を 招く 可能性 が ある の です 。 
 また 、 収益 成長率 に対する 株価 の 比率 を 示す 指標 も 3 倍 を 超え て おり 、 通常 の 投資 基準 から する と 割高 な 状態 です 。 これ は 長期 的 な 投資 として の 魅力 を 減じる 要因 と なって います 。 
 最近 では 先端 技術 関連 銘柄 全体 に対する 市場 の 熱狂 が やや 冷静 化し て おり 、 2025 年 初め から 約 5 % の 株価 下落 が 見 られ ます 。 投資家 の 関心 が 評価 水準 へ の 懸念 に 移行 すれ ば 、 売却 圧力 が 強まる 恐れ があります 。 
 出典 ： マネックス証券 マネ クリ

10.title: What Palantir’s New Partnerships Reveal About Its Future | Markets Insider
10.content:
what palantir ’s new partnerships reveal about its future 
 palantir technologies ( pltr ) has been busy lately with some big moves and partnerships spanning various industries . lately , it seems like palantir is teaming up with someone new every time we check the headlines . one thing is certain , palantir is planting its ai - powered flag in nearly every major industry , from national defense to healthcare , aviation , and utilities . but what do all these deals mean , and where is palantir headed ? in this piece , we ’ll try to make sense of the strategy behind this cluster of plays . 
 light up your portfolio with spark : 
 easily identify stocks ' risks and opportunities . 
 discover stocks ' market position with detailed competitor analyses . 
 so , what ’s going on at palantir ? 
 in the past few months , palantir has struck several strategic deals that show it ’s no longer a government contractor . it ’s positioning itself as the go - to ai platform for industries that need to make fast , data - driven decisions , from war zones to hospital labs . these aren’t small announcements , either . each deal targets a specific industry and paints a much bigger picture of palantir ’s future . 
 here ’s a look at the key partnerships and how they play into the company ’s long game : 
 palantir and ever fox 
 palantir partnered with ever fox to boost command - and - control systems in highly secure military environments . the idea was to combine palantir ’s mission manager ai with everfox ’s security tech to help soldiers and analysts process data from multiple sensors in real time . this strengthens palantir ’s grip on defense contracts , reinforcing its role as a critical player in modern warfare technology . 
 palantir and saur group 
 in a totally different sector , palantir partnered with saur , a french utility company that manages water and wastewater treatment . saur uses palantir foundry ’s generative ai to streamline contract management and compliance tracking . this shows how palantir ’s ai can be adapted beyond defense and into public infrastructure , cutting red tape and saving time in industries that are usually not synonymous with innovation . 
 palantir and parexel 
 although this partnership with parexel , a clinical research organization , is almost deemed old news as it was struck in april 2024 , it did give palantir a foothold in the healthcare sector and is part of palantir ’s broader plan . the goal is to speed up drug development using ai to manage trials , track data , and comply with safety rules . it ’s no secret that the pharmaceutical industry moves slowly , and palantir offers a way to fast - track drug procedures without cutting corners . that could mean significant revenue from healthcare in the years ahead . 
 palantir and databricks 
 palantir also joined forces with databricks , a heavyweight in data engineering . together , they ’re integrating their platforms to offer more powerful ai and data tools to clients in healthcare and beyond . this is about creating a bigger ecosystem . by linking up with databricks , palantir makes it easier for companies to adopt its ai tools without replacing their existing systems .

 - benefit # 2 : building trust and credibility . b corp certification provides a clear and credible signal to the market that a company is serious about its social and environmental responsibilities . by publicly disclosing its b impact report , a company can demonstrate its transparency and accountability to its stakeholders . for example , ben & jerry ' s , a b corp since 2012 , uses its b impact report to communicate its progress and challenges in areas such as sourcing , emissions , and diversity . 
 - benefit # 3 : joining a global community . b corp certification connects a company to a network of over 4,000 b corps across 77 countries and 153 industries , who share best practices , collaborate on projects , and advocate for systemic change . by being part of this community , a company can access valuable resources , opportunities , and support . for example , natura , a b corp since 2014 , is a brazilian cosmetics company that has partnered with other b corps to promote the circular economy and the amazon biome conservation . 
 - challenge # 1 : meeting the high standards . b corp certification is not easy to achieve or maintain . a company must score at least 80 out of 200 points on the b impact assessment , which covers five areas : governance , workers , customers , community , and environment . a company must also amend its legal structure to incorporate its social and environmental commitments . for example , kickstarter , a b corp since 2015 , is a public benefit corporation , which means it has a legal duty to consider the impact of its decisions on society , not just shareholders . 
 - challenge # 2 : balancing profit and purpose . b corp certification does not mean that a company has to sacrifice its financial performance for its social and environmental impact . rather , it means that a company has to find a way to create value for all its stakeholders , not just shareholders . this may require a company to make trade - offs , invest in long - term initiatives , and innovate its business model . for example , danone , a b corp since 2018 , is a global food company that has committed to become carbon neutral by 2050 , which involves transforming its supply chain , product portfolio , and packaging . 
 2. how it can boost your brand , impact , and profitability ? 
 boost your brand 
 becoming a certified b corporation is not only a way to demonstrate your commitment to social and environmental responsibility , but also a smart business strategy that can give you a competitive edge in the market . by meeting the highest standards of performance , accountability , and transparency , you can attract more customers , investors , employees , and partners who share your values and vision . here are some of the benefits of b corp certification that can boost your brand , impact , and profitability : 
 - increase your brand awareness and reputation . b corp certification is a globally recognized seal of trust and excellence that signals your company 's positive impact and differentiation . according to a 2019 study by b lab , the nonprofit organization that certifies b corps , 72% of consumers are more likely to trust a b corp than a non - certified business , and 68 % are more likely to buy from a b corp. moreover , b corp certification can help you gain exposure and recognition from various media outlets , awards , and rankings that showcase the best b corps in the world . 
 - enhance your customer loyalty and retention . b corp certification can help you build a loyal customer base that values your purpose and mission . by aligning your products or services with the needs and aspirations of your target audience , you can create a strong emotional connection and a sense of belonging . for example , patagonia , a leading outdoor clothing and gear company and a certified b corp , has a loyal fan base that appreciates its environmental activism and high - quality products . patagonia also engages its customers in various campaigns and initiatives that support its social and environmental causes , such as donating 1 % of its sales to grassroots organizations , encouraging customers to repair and reuse their products , and suing the trump administration for reducing the size of national monuments . 
 - attract and retain top talent . b corp certification can help you attract and retain talented and motivated employees who want to work for a company that makes a positive difference in the world . by offering a meaningful and fulfilling work environment , you can foster a culture of engagement , collaboration , and innovation . according to a 2018 report by b lab , b corps have 25 % higher employee satisfaction and retention rates than other businesses , and 77 % of b corp employees report being highly engaged at work , compared to 33 % of the global workforce . additionally , b corp certification can help you access various resources and networks that can support your talent development , such as the b hive online platform , the b corp leadership development program , and the b corp academic community . 
 - access new markets and opportunities . b corp certification can help you expand your market reach and opportunities by connecting you with other b corps , partners , and stakeholders who share your values and goals . by joining the b corp community , you can access a global network of over 4,000 b corps across 77 countries and 150 industries , and collaborate with them on various projects , campaigns , and events . you can also leverage the b corp brand and certification to enter new markets and segments that are looking for sustainable and responsible businesses . for example , danone , one of the world 's largest food and beverage companies and a certified b corp , has used its b corp status to enter the growing market of conscious consumers who demand healthier and more ethical products . danone has also partnered with other b corps , such as happy family organics and alter eco , to co - create and distribute new products that meet the b corp standards . 
 3. how to meet the rigorous standards and requirements ? 
 becoming a certified b corporation is not an easy task . it requires a company to undergo a rigorous assessment process that evaluates its social and environmental performance , accountability , and transparency . the assessment covers five areas : governance , workers , customers , community , and environment . each area has a set of standards and requirements that the company must meet or exceed to qualify for the certification . some of the challenges that a company may face in meeting these standards and requirements are : 
 - governance : the company must demonstrate that it has a clear mission and vision that aligns with the b corp values of creating positive impact for all stakeholders . the company must also have a board of directors that oversees its strategic direction and ensures its accountability to its mission and stakeholders . the company must disclose its ownership structure , governance practices , and policies on issues such as diversity , equity , and inclusion , anti - corruption , and whistleblowing . the company must also adopt the b corp legal framework , which requires it to amend its articles of incorporation or bylaws to include a commitment to balance the interests of all stakeholders , not just shareholders , in its decision - making . 
 - workers : the company must treat its employees fairly and respectfully , and provide them with a safe , healthy , and supportive work environment . the company must pay its workers a living wage , offer them benefits such as health insurance , retirement plans , and paid leave , and ensure that they have opportunities for professional development and career advancement . the company must also foster a culture of trust , engagement , and empowerment among its workers , and solicit their feedback and input on its performance and impact . the company must measure and report on its employee satisfaction , turnover , diversity , and compensation . 
 - customers : the company must offer products or services that create value for its customers and address their needs and preferences . the company must also ensure that its products or services are of high quality , safe , and ethical , and that they do not harm the environment or society . the company must communicate honestly and transparently with its customers , and respect their privacy and data rights . the company must also seek to educate its customers about its mission and impact , and encourage them to join its movement for positive change . the company must measure and report on its customer satisfaction , loyalty , and feedback . 
 - community : the company must be a good citizen and a positive force in the communities where it operates . the company must respect and support the local culture , economy , and environment , and contribute to the social and environmental well - being of its community members . the company must also engage with and support other b corps and social enterprises , and collaborate with them to amplify their collective impact . the company must measure and report on its community involvement , donations , volunteering , advocacy , and partnerships . 
 - environment : the company must minimize its negative environmental impact and maximize its positive environmental impact . the company must adopt sustainable practices and policies that reduce its greenhouse gas emissions , energy consumption , water use , waste generation , and pollution . the company must also use renewable or recycled materials and resources , and design its products or services to be durable , reusable , or recyclable . the company must also protect and restore the natural habitats and biodiversity that it affects or depends on . the company must measure and report on its environmental footprint , performance , and goals . 
 these are some of the challenges that a company may face in meeting the rigorous standards and requirements of b corp certification . however , these challenges are also opportunities for the company to improve its performance and impact , and to differentiate itself from its competitors . by becoming a certified b corp , the company can join a global community of leaders and innovators who are using business as a force for good . the company can also gain access to various benefits and resources that can help it grow and thrive in the long term . the company can also inspire and influence other businesses , consumers , and policymakers to join the movement for a more inclusive and sustainable economy . 
 4. how to apply , assess , and verify your performance ? 
 becoming a certified b corporation is not a simple or quick process . it requires a commitment to meet the highest standards of social and environmental performance , accountability , and transparency . the certification process involves three main steps : applying , assessing , and verifying . each step has its own challenges and benefits , and it is important to understand them before embarking on this journey . 
 1. applying : the first step is to complete the online b impact assessment ( bia ) , which measures the impact of your company on your workers , customers , community , and environment . the bia is a free and confidential tool that helps you benchmark your performance against other businesses and identify areas for improvement . you need to score at least 80 out of 200 points to qualify for certification . you can also use the bia as a learning and management tool , regardless of whether you pursue certification or not . 
 2. assessing : the second step is to review your bia results and submit them for evaluation by b lab , the non - profit organization that administers the certification . b lab will verify the accuracy and completeness of your answers , and may ask for additional documentation or clarification . you will also need to complete a disclosure questionnaire , which covers any sensitive issues or negative impacts that your company may have . b lab will use this information to determine if there are any red flags that could prevent you from becoming certified . 
 3. verifying : the third step is to undergo a verification process , which includes a phone call with a b lab staff member and a site visit by a third - party reviewer . the verification process is designed to confirm that your practices match your responses on the bia and the disclosure questionnaire , and that you meet the legal requirements for certification . you will also need to sign the b corp declaration of interdependence and the b corp agreement , which formalize your commitment to the b corp community and the certification standards . once you pass the verification process , you will receive your certification and join the global network of b corps . 
 becoming a certified b corp is not easy , but it is rewarding . it can help you differentiate your brand , attract and retain talent , access new markets and capital , and create positive social and environmental change . for example , patagonia , a leading outdoor clothing and gear company , became a certified b corp in 2011 to align its values with its legal structure and to inspire other businesses to do the same . patagonia has since increased its sales , improved its employee engagement , and reduced its environmental footprint . by becoming a certified b corp , you can also demonstrate your leadership and credibility in the corporate world and beyond .

 these are some of the best practices that you can follow to learn from and collaborate with other certified businesses and make the most of your b corp certification . by doing so , you can not only improve your own performance and impact , but also contribute to the collective success and growth of the b corp movement . 
 6. how it can shape the corporate landscape and influence policy ? 
 as more and more businesses adopt the b corp certification , they are not only demonstrating their commitment to social and environmental responsibility , but also creating a positive impact on the corporate landscape and influencing policy . the b corp certification has the potential to shape the future of business in several ways , such as : 
 - creating a network of like - minded businesses that can collaborate , share best practices , and support each other in their sustainability goals . for example , the b corp community has launched initiatives such as the b corp climate collective , which aims to mobilize b corps to take action on climate change and reduce their greenhouse gas emissions .

3.title: What is B Corp, and should our business apply? — Bold Green Strategies | London Sustainability Consultancy

what is b corp , and should our business apply ? 
 16 may 
 written by nash gierak 
 sustainability consultant + strategist nash gierak gives us a rundown of the benefits and challenges that businesses should consider when aiming to become an accredited “ force for good . ” 
 introduction 
 if you 're looking to start a business or want to make your existing company more socially responsible , you may have heard of b corp certification . b corp is a certification given to businesses that meet high standards of social and environmental performance , accountability , and transparency . in this blog post , we 'll explore what b corp is , why it 's important , and whether or not your business should pursue certification . 
 benefits of b corp certification 
 b corp certification has several benefits for businesses . first and foremost , it provides a framework for companies to measure their impact on the environment , their employees , and the communities they serve . by setting clear standards and guidelines , b corp certification ensures that businesses are held accountable for their impact on society . additionally , b corp certification can help businesses stand out in an increasingly crowded market . consumers and investors are more likely to support companies that are transparent about their social and environmental impact , which can lead to increased revenue and growth opportunities . finally , b corp certification can help attract and retain talented employees who are passionate about working for a socially responsible business . 
 challenges of b corp certification 
 while there are many benefits to becoming a b corp , there are also some challenges that businesses may face . the most significant challenge is the cost and time commitment required to obtain certification . the certification process can be lengthy and expensive ( this is on a sliding scale though ) , and it requires businesses to make significant changes to their operations to meet the rigorous standards set by b lab . additionally , some businesses may be hesitant to pursue certification because they fear it will negatively impact their bottom line . however , it 's worth noting that many businesses see a return on investment from pursuing b corp certification , both in terms of increased revenue and improved employee retention . 
 there has also been some criticism towards b corp. this was due to some some companies with less - than - ideal reputations qualifying for the certification . you can have a read about that here . this triggered a consultation and review which has addressed these concerns ( and even resulted in a business losing their certification ) reassuring consumers , clients , and the members of the b corp community that really are committed to social and environmental change . you can read the report here . 
 should your business apply to b corp 
 ultimately , the decision to pursue b corp certification is up to each individual business . however , if your company is committed to social and environmental responsibility , pursuing certification can be a valuable way to demonstrate that commitment to your stakeholders . if you 're unsure about whether or not to pursue certification , consider reaching out to other b corps in your industry to learn more about their experiences and the impact certification has had on their businesses . additionally , you can take the b impact assessment , a free tool that allows you to assess your business 's impact and see how it measures up against the b corp standards . 
 green washers take note ! b corp should never be a tickbox exercise for businesses . as you will have read above , this is a widely recognised certification , and as such , is widely talked about in the media . this is a great thing for ethical businesses , but not so great for unethical ones ! 
 how bold green strategies can help 
 b corp certification is a way for businesses to demonstrate their commitment to social and environmental responsibility . while there are challenges associated with obtaining certification , the benefits can outweigh the costs for businesses that are serious about making a positive impact on society . ultimately , the decision to pursue certification is up to each individual business , but it is clear that b corp certification is becoming increasingly important for companies that want to be leaders in the movement towards a more sustainable and equitable future . 
 if you have b corp in your sights , bold green strategies will perform a gap analysis of your business , and will provide an interactive checklist to ensure your score meets the required 80 points ( we always shoot for a minimum safety net of 90 ! ) . this will give you the opportunity to collate the relevant documentation for existing frameworks and policies . if you fall under the minimum score — as most businesses will — we will provide you with a suite of creative options to boost your application ( and your business in the process ! ) . we can tweak your sustainability strategy to reflect these changes , and can train your team in how to implement and communicate the accreditation . 
 to start your b corp journey , drop us a line at hello @ bold green strategies . com and we ’ll be happy to talk you through it all in more detail !

 5. community engagement : being part of the b corp community provides opportunities for collaboration and learning from other mission - driven businesses .

 the b corp movement is redefining success in business . it 's not just about being the best in the world , but about being the best for the world . as startups strive to carve out their niche , b corp certification stands as a testament to their dedication to making a positive impact on society and the planet . it 's a powerful way to build credibility , trust , and a loyal customer base that shares the company 's values . for startups looking to make a difference , the b corp certification is more than a badge—it 's a statement of purpose and a commitment to a better future .

the b corp certification

 what is the b corp certification and why should you get the certification ? 
 the b corporation ( b corp ) certification is a third - party standard that allows companies to meet their highest standards of social and environmental impact , verified by transparency and accountability towards their stakeholders . 
 this certification is issued by b lab , a non - profit organisation founded in 2006 in the united states , with the scope of transforming the global economy to benefit all people , communities , and the planet . 
 quite curiously the " b " is not an evaluation score but stands for beneficial . therefore , it means that the certified organizations meet their standards of transparency , accountability , sustainability on a voluntary base . 
 the benefits of obtaining a b corp are multiple and holistic . 
 first , it helps to build trust with consumers , communities , and suppliers . in fact , high transparency and accountability standards increase both confidence and visibility as a brand . 
 further , the certification attracts and retain more sustainable - minded employees ; and draws mission - aligned investors . finally , consequently to such benefits , as a uk study shows the b corp busines grow 28 times faster than uk average . 
 as of march 2024 , there are 8 , 324 certified b corporations across 162 industries in 96 countries . 
 the pathway to certification 
 the process to achieve and maintain certification is rigorous and requires engaging teams and departments across the company . the pathway will vary depending on few factors , as revenue and company size , sector , industry , and ownership structure . 
 if you work with a start-up or smaller company , your certification process will be based on a pending b corporation ; whereas if you work in a company , the certification guide is based on the size of the enterprise : small , small - medium , medium or large . 
 to obtain the b corporation certification , an entity first needs to register and complete the risk review . following , is the b impact assessment ( bia ) , which measures the positive impact of the company in areas of governance , workers , community , the environment . to pass the assessment , all companies need to earn a minimum score of 80 out of 200 points to further proceed to the other steps . 
 after establishing the enterprise profile , you can learn about your baseline score : if it is under the 80 - point benchmark , you must revaluate and prioritize improvement areas . whereas , if it ’s over the 80 - point benchmark , you can submit your bia for review . 
 once the evaluation and verification queues are completed , you will have the opportunity to sign the b corp agreement and therefore reached the final step : the certification . meeting the transparency requirement for b corp certification means that you’ll need to publish your public profile in the b corp directory , including your company ’s score and impact report . 
 the certification lasts for 3 years , after which the enterprise is required to prepare for recertification , where can rely on the bia and the certification process as a tool for continuous improvement . 
 how does the b impact assessment work ? 
 used by more than 150,000 businesses , the bia is a digital tool that evaluates how your company ’s operations and business model impact your workers , community , environment , and customers . 
 the assessment covers the company 's entire operation and measures the positive impact of the company in 5 areas : governance , workers , community , environment , as well as the products or services the company provides . 
 b impact assessment structure 
 to fulfil this step , you have to answer a series of questions - approximately 200 – regarding the business practices and outputs . questions you can expect are “ what is the percentage of management from underrepresented populations ? ” , “ does your company monitor and record its universal waste production ? ” or “ how do you verify that your product improves the impact of your client organizations ? ” . 
 following , you can see where your business is outperforming others , and where there ’s room for improvement . this way , you can identify , track , and learn about improvement opportunities and best practices . 
 furthermore , since certified enterprises are required to undergo the verification process every three years to renew the certification , b corps also helps to continuously improve the company ’s standards , leading to long - term resiliency . 
 b corp certification is holistic , not exclusively focused on a single social or environmental issue .

 in the landscape of modern business , where consumers are increasingly conscious of the ethical footprint of their purchases , b - corp certification stands out as a distinctive mark of a company 's commitment to not just profit , but also to social and environmental responsibility . this certification , awarded by the non - profit b lab , requires businesses to meet rigorous standards of social and environmental performance , accountability , and transparency . for startups , obtaining b - corp certification can be a transformative step , one that elevates their brand identity significantly . it signals to customers , investors , and partners that the company is dedicated to higher standards of purpose and performance , setting them apart in a crowded marketplace . 
 1. enhanced consumer trust : a b - corp badge on products or services acts as a seal of trust , assuring consumers that the company operates with a commitment to social and environmental excellence . for example , patagonia , a certified b - corp , has built a loyal customer base partly due to its environmental advocacy and sustainable practices . 
 2. attracting impact investors : startups with b - corp certification often find it easier to attract impact investors who are looking to put their money into businesses that align with their values . bain capital 's double impact fund , for instance , focuses on investing in companies that are certified b - corps or are committed to becoming one . 
 3. employee engagement and retention : companies that are b - corp certified often report higher levels of employee satisfaction and retention . employees today want to work for organizations that reflect their values . etsy , another b - corp , has been recognized for its employee - friendly policies and inclusive culture . 
 4. differentiation in the market : b - corp certification helps startups stand out from competitors by highlighting their commitment to more than just profit . this differentiation can be a key factor in a consumer 's decision - making process . allbirds , the shoe company , uses its b - corp status to differentiate its brand in the highly competitive footwear industry . 
 5. building community and networking : being part of the b - corp community provides access to a network of like - minded companies and entrepreneurs . this community can be a valuable resource for collaboration , learning , and support . the annual b - corp champions retreat is one such event that brings together leaders from certified companies worldwide . 
 6. long - term value creation : while the certification process is rigorous and often challenging for a startup , the long - term benefits include creating a sustainable business model that can lead to long - term value creation . danone north america , a large b - corp , has shown that sustainable practices can go hand - in - hand with profitability and growth . 
 b - corp certification is more than a badge—it 's a statement of a company 's ethos and a blueprint for its operations . it 's a commitment that resonates with all stakeholders and weaves into the very fabric of the brand 's identity , promising not only financial success but also a positive impact on society and the environment . for startups , it 's a powerful way to build a brand that people believe in and want to support . 
 how b corp certification elevates brand identity - the importance of b corp certification for startups 
 4. the competitive advantage of being a b - corp certified startup 
 achieving b - corp certification is a significant milestone for any startup . it 's a rigorous process that not only measures a company 's social and environmental performance but also its commitment to transparency and accountability . startups that become b - corp certified join an elite group of businesses that have met the highest standards of verified performance . this certification can be a powerful differentiator in a crowded market , signaling to customers , investors , and employees that the company is serious about its mission to do good . 
 from a competitive standpoint , b - corp certification can provide several advantages : 
 1. brand differentiation : in a marketplace where consumers are increasingly values - driven , b - corp certification sets a startup apart as a leader in ethical business practices . for example , patagonia 's commitment to sustainability and ethical manufacturing has helped it cultivate a loyal customer base . 
 2. attracting talent : many job seekers prioritize companies with strong social and environmental commitments . b - corp certification can help attract top talent who are looking for more than just a paycheck . the certification can be particularly appealing to millennials and gen z workers who want their work to have a positive impact . 
 3. investor interest : impact investing is on the rise , and b - corp certification can make a startup more attractive to investors who are looking to put their money into businesses that are making a positive difference . for instance , kickstarter 's decision to become a public benefit corporation ( which overlaps with b - corp values ) was well - received by socially conscious investors . 
 4. operational improvements : the process of becoming certified requires a deep look into a company 's operations , which can lead to improvements in efficiency and sustainability . these improvements can reduce costs and improve margins over time . 
 5. networking opportunities : being part of the b - corp community provides access to a network of like - minded businesses and entrepreneurs . this can lead to partnerships , collaborations , and new business opportunities . 
 6. customer loyalty : customers who choose to support b - corp businesses are often highly engaged and loyal . they appreciate the company 's commitment to higher standards and are more likely to become repeat customers . 
 7. regulatory support : in some regions , b - corps may benefit from legal protections , tax benefits , or procurement preferences that support their business models . 
 8. long - term resilience : companies that are built to be sustainable and socially responsible are often better positioned to weather economic downturns and shifts in consumer preferences . 
 by integrating social and environmental goals into their core business strategies , b - corp certified startups not only contribute to a better world but also build a strong foundation for long - term success . the certification is not just a badge—it 's a commitment to continuous improvement and a way to build a business that stands for something greater than profit alone .

 5. the process and its impact on operations 
 b - corp certification represents a significant milestone for any startup aiming to align its operations with social and environmental performance , accountability , and transparency . this certification goes beyond product or service - level certification ; it 's a holistic recognition of a company 's commitment to higher standards of purpose and the integration of stakeholder interests into core business practices . the process of obtaining b - corp certification is rigorous and transformative , often serving as a catalyst for operational changes that resonate through every level of the organization . it begins with an assessment that measures a company 's impact on its workers , customers , community , and environment . this evaluation is not just a checklist but a deep dive into the company 's governance structure and impact footprint , pushing companies to not only be the best in the world but the best for the world . 
 from the perspective of a startup founder , the journey towards certification is one of introspection and alignment . it requires a critical look at current practices and a willingness to pivot towards more sustainable and equitable operations . for employees , it often translates into better working conditions and a sense of pride in contributing to a company that stands for more than just profit . customers and investors , on the other hand , may view b - corp certification as a seal of trust and a commitment to long - term value creation that goes beyond financial returns . 
 here 's an in - depth look at the certification process and its operational impacts : 
 1. eligibility assessment : startups must first ensure they meet the basic requirements for certification , which includes being in operation for at least a year . this period allows for the accumulation of enough operational data to assess performance . 
 2. b impact assessment : companies must complete the b impact assessment ( bia ) , a comprehensive tool that evaluates a company 's impact on its workers , community , environment , and customers . the assessment scores companies out of 200 points , and a minimum of 80 is required to pass . 
 3. documentation & verification : after completing the bia , companies must provide documentation to support their answers . this step is followed by a review process where b lab staff verify the responses and may request additional documentation or conduct interviews . 
 4. improvement plan : if a company doesn't score the required 80 points , it must create an improvement plan to increase its score . this often involves operational changes , such as implementing new hr policies or environmental programs . 
 5. legal accountability : to finalize certification , companies must amend their legal governing documents to reflect their commitment to balancing profit and purpose by considering the impact of their decisions on all stakeholders . 
 6. certification fee : there 's a fee for certification , scaled to the company 's annual sales , ensuring that the process is accessible to startups of varying sizes . 
 7. recertification : b - corp certification isn't a one - time achievement . companies must recertify every three years , demonstrating continuous improvement . 
 for example , patagonia , the outdoor clothing brand , has been a b - corp since 2011 . their certification has influenced operations from supply chain management to product design , ensuring that environmental and social responsibility are embedded in every decision . 
 the b - corp certification process is a challenging yet rewarding journey that can redefine a startup 's operations and brand identity . it 's a commitment to an ongoing process of improvement and accountability that can set a company apart in a crowded marketplace , attracting customers , employees , and investors who share a vision for a more inclusive and sustainable economy .

 6. the financial benefits of b - corp status 
 attracting investors is a pivotal moment for any startup , and achieving b - corp certification can be a significant milestone in that journey . this certification not only signals a company 's commitment to social and environmental responsibility but also opens the door to a niche market of impact investors who are looking to support businesses that align with their values . from a financial standpoint , b - corp status can enhance a company 's appeal to a broader investor base , potentially leading to increased funding opportunities . it 's a mark of trust and sustainability that can differentiate a startup in a crowded marketplace . 
 1. enhanced brand reputation : investors are increasingly drawn to companies that demonstrate ethical practices and sustainable business models . b - corp certification serves as a testament to a company 's dedication to these principles , which can lead to increased investor confidence and potentially higher valuations . 
 2. access to impact investment funds : there are funds specifically dedicated to investing in socially responsible businesses . b - corp status can provide startups with access to these funds , which might otherwise be inaccessible . 
 3. tax incentives : in some jurisdictions , certified b - corps may be eligible for tax benefits , which can improve a startup 's financial health and make it more attractive to investors . 
 4. customer loyalty : a growing segment of consumers prefers to do business with companies that are socially responsible . this loyalty can translate into consistent revenue streams and a solid business case for investors . 
 5. employee attraction and retention : companies with strong social and environmental commitments often find it easier to attract and retain top talent . this can lead to lower recruitment costs and higher productivity , both of which are attractive to investors . 
 for example , patagonia , a well - known outdoor clothing brand , has leveraged its b - corp status to attract investors who are interested in supporting a company with a proven track record of environmental stewardship . this has not only helped them secure investments but also build a loyal customer base that values their commitment to sustainability . 
 b - corp certification can offer startups a competitive edge when attracting investors . it 's a clear indicator of a company 's commitment to more than just profit , resonating with a growing trend of ethical investment and consumerism . startups that achieve this status may find themselves better positioned to secure the financial backing they need to grow and succeed .

 7. building a sustainable business model with b - corp principles 
 building a sustainable business

 building a sustainable business model 
 embracing b - corp principles is akin to setting the compass of a startup towards sustainability and ethical business practices . it 's not merely about adhering to a set of standards ; it 's about integrating a philosophy that values environmental stewardship , social responsibility , and transparency alongside profitability . this holistic approach to business is what sets b - corps apart , offering a blueprint for companies that aspire to be not just the best in the world , but the best for the world . by building a business model around these principles , startups can create a robust framework that supports sustainable growth , attracts like - minded investors and employees , and fosters a loyal customer base that shares their values . 
 1. stakeholder integration : unlike traditional business models that prioritize shareholder value , b - corps operate under the legal framework of stakeholder integration . this means decisions are made considering the impact on all stakeholders , including employees , customers , suppliers , community , and the environment . for example , patagonia , the outdoor clothing brand , has been a pioneer in this aspect , investing in sustainable materials and fair labor practices , which has paid dividends in customer loyalty and brand reputation . 
 2. environmental performance : a core tenet of b - corp certification is environmental performance . startups must demonstrate a commitment to reducing their ecological footprint through sustainable practices . method , a company known for eco-friendly cleaning products , has set an example by ensuring its ingredients are biodegradable and its packaging is recyclable , thus minimizing its environmental impact . 
 3. social impact : b - corps are also evaluated on their social impact . this includes providing fair wages , supporting community initiatives , and fostering diversity and inclusion . greyston bakery , for instance , employs an open hiring policy that provides jobs to individuals regardless of their background , contributing to social equity and community development . 
 4. transparency and accountability : transparency is a hallmark of b - corp certification . companies must publish detailed reports on their social and environmental performance . this level of accountability builds trust with consumers and stakeholders . for example , the footwear company allbirds discloses its carbon footprint for each product , demonstrating its commitment to transparency and accountability . 
 5. continuous improvement : the b - corp assessment isn't a one - time achievement ; it requires continuous improvement . businesses must recertify every three years , showing progress in their sustainable practices . this encourages a culture of ongoing development and innovation . 
 adopting b - corp principles is not just a strategic move for startups ; it 's a commitment to a set of values that resonate with a growing segment of the market that demands ethical and sustainable business practices . as consumers become more conscious of the impact of their purchases , startups with b - corp certification may find themselves with a competitive edge , poised for long - term success in an increasingly conscientious marketplace . building a sustainable business model with b - corp principles is , therefore , both a moral imperative and a strategic business decision . it 's a journey that requires dedication , innovation , and a willingness to challenge the status quo , but the rewards are manifold and extend far beyond the bottom line . 
 building a sustainable business model with b corp principles - the importance of b corp certification for startups 
 8. the role of b - corp in cultivating community and customer loyalty 
 b - corp certification is more than a mere badge of honor for startups ; it 's a commitment to a set of values that resonate deeply with both the community and customers . this certification signals a company 's dedication to not just profit but also to the planet and its people . it 's a holistic approach to business that considers the long - term impacts of decisions and actions . by aligning their operations with the rigorous standards set by b - lab , b - corps inherently foster a sense of trust and loyalty among their stakeholders . this trust is not easily won ; it comes from consistent , transparent actions and a genuine commitment to community welfare and environmental stewardship . 
 1. community engagement : b - corps often lead by example , showing that businesses can be a force for good . take , for instance , patagonia , a certified b - corp known for its environmental activism . by donating time , money , and resources to conservation efforts , patagonia has built a community of loyal customers who share their values . 
 2. employee satisfaction : happy employees often translate to happy customers . b - corps like etsy create a positive work environment with policies that support work - life balance , which in turn reflects in the quality of customer service and product innovation . 
 3. transparency : transparency is key in building trust . b - corps are required to produce an annual impact report detailing their social and environmental performance , which helps customers understand the company 's values and practices . 
 4. sustainable practices : by committing to sustainable practices , b - corps like allbirds have attracted a 
 customer base 
 that prioritizes environmental responsibility , thus fostering a loyal community that supports their mission . 
 5. quality products and services : b - corps are often synonymous with quality . by refusing to cut corners , companies like bombas deliver products that customers are proud to use and recommend . 
 6. inclusive business models : b - corps often incorporate inclusivity into their business model . for example , greyston bakery operates on an ' open hiring ' policy , which has garnered immense support from customers who value social equity . 
 7. customer engagement : b - corps actively involve customers in their mission . whether it 's through volunteer programs or customer feedback loops , companies like warby parker ensure that their customers ' voices are heard and valued . 
 b - corp certification is a powerful tool for startups looking to build a loyal community and customer base . by adhering to the principles of social and environmental performance , accountability , and transparency , b - corps can create a strong , positive brand image that resonates with consumers and employees alike , leading to a sustainable and profitable business model . 
 the role of b corp in cultivating community and customer loyalty - the importance of b corp certification for startups 
 9. the future of startups and b - corp certification 
 as we gaze into the horizon of the entrepreneurial landscape , the integration of b - corp certification into the startup ecosystem emerges as a beacon of sustainable business practices . this evolution reflects a growing recognition that long - term success is not solely measured by financial gain but also by the positive impact on society and the environment . startups , often agile and innovative by nature , are increasingly aligning their operations with the values encapsulated by b - corp certification . this shift is not just a trend but a profound transformation in the foundational ethos of new businesses . 
 1. holistic business metrics : b - corp certification requires companies to meet rigorous standards of social and environmental performance , accountability , and transparency . for startups , this means adopting a framework that evaluates more than the bottom line . for example , ' allbirds ' , a footwear company , has embedded environmental responsibility into its core , using sustainable materials and committing to carbon neutrality . 
 2. investor appeal : the future of startups is also shaped by investor preferences . a b - corp certification can be a powerful signal to potential investors that a startup is committed to more than just profit . ' patagonia ' , an outdoor apparel company , has long been a b - corp and is often cited as a model for balancing profitability with environmental stewardship , attracting like - minded investors . 
 3. consumer trust : as consumers become more conscious of their purchasing power , startups with b - corp certification may enjoy increased brand loyalty and trust . ' ben & jerry ' s ' , while no longer a startup , exemplifies how a commitment to social causes can resonate with customers and create a strong , loyal community . 
 4. talent attraction and retention : the workforce , especially millennials and gen z , is increasingly looking to work for companies that reflect their values . b - corp certification can help startups attract and retain talent who are not only skilled but also passionate about their employer 's mission . ' etsy ' , the online marketplace for handmade goods , has leveraged its b - corp status to attract employees who are enthusiastic about sustainability and community . 
 5. regulatory landscape : with governments around the world beginning to recognize the importance of sustainable business practices , the regulatory environment is becoming more favorable for b - corps . this could lead to incentives and support for certified startups , further encouraging the adoption of b - corp principles . 
 6. collaborative networks : b - corps are part of a global community of leaders that drive a global movement of people using business as a force for good . this network can provide startups with valuable connections , mentorship , and collaboration opportunities . ' danone north america ' , a large b - corp , has shown how collaboration within the b - corp community can lead to innovative solutions to shared challenges . 
 the trajectory for startups seems inextricably linked with the principles of b - corp certification . as this movement grows , it 's likely that the startups of tomorrow will not just be judged by their innovative products or services , but also by their ability to foster an inclusive economy that works for everyone . the future is bright for startups that embrace this ethos , and b - corp certification stands as a testament to their commitment to not just being the best in the world , but the best for the world .
