 2. what are the different ways to collaborate with startups and other partners ? 
 corporate venturing is a strategic approach to innovation that involves collaborating with external partners , such as startups , universities , research institutes , or other corporations , to access new technologies , markets , or capabilities . corporate venturing can take various forms and models , depending on the goals , resources , and culture of the corporation and its partners . in this section , we will explore some of the most common and effective types and models of corporate venturing , and how they can help corporations achieve their innovation vision and objectives . 
 some of the types and models of corporate venturing are : 
 1. corporate venture capital ( cvc ) : this is the most prevalent and well - known form of corporate venturing , where a corporation invests in startups that are relevant to its core business or strategic interests . the corporation can provide financial , technical , or operational support to the startups , and in return , gain access to their innovations , insights , or networks . cvc can also help the corporation scout for potential acquisition targets , or create synergies with its existing businesses . for example , google ventures , the cvc arm of google , has invested in hundreds of startups across various sectors , such as uber , slack , stripe , and 23 and me , and has helped them grow and scale their products and services . 
 2. corporate incubators and accelerators : these are programs that provide startups with mentorship , training , resources , and funding to help them develop and validate their ideas , products , or business models . the corporation can benefit from the fresh and diverse perspectives of the startups , and also identify potential partners or customers for its own products or services . corporate incubators and accelerators can be run internally by the corporation , or externally by a third - party partner . for example , microsoft for startups , the corporate accelerator program of microsoft , offers startups access to its cloud platform , technical expertise , and global network , and has helped them generate over $ 3 billion in revenue . 
 3. corporate venturing partnerships : these are strategic alliances or joint ventures between a corporation and one or more external partners , such as other corporations , universities , research institutes , or government agencies , to collaborate on a specific project , challenge , or opportunity . the corporation can leverage the complementary skills , assets , or resources of its partners , and also share the risks and rewards of the collaboration . corporate venturing partnerships can enable the corporation to enter new markets , create new products or services , or solve complex problems . for example , ibm , the global technology company , has partnered with mit , the leading research university , to create the mit - ibm watson ai lab , a joint research center that focuses on advancing artificial intelligence for social and business impact . 
 what are the different ways to collaborate with startups and other partners - corporate venturing strategy : how to define and execute your innovation vision and objectives 
 3. how to measure and evaluate your innovation performance and impact ? 
 one of the most important aspects of corporate venturing is to define and track the success factors and metrics that reflect the innovation performance and impact of the ventures . these metrics should be aligned with the strategic objectives and vision of the corporate venturing unit , as well as the overall corporate goals and values . however , measuring and evaluating innovation is not a straightforward or simple process , as there are many different dimensions and perspectives to consider . in this section , we will explore some of the key challenges and best practices for developing and using innovation metrics in corporate venturing , and provide some examples of how leading companies have done so . 
 some of the main challenges and questions that corporate venturers face when defining and measuring innovation are : 
 - how to balance the short - term and long - term outcomes and impacts of the ventures ? innovation often requires a longer time horizon and a higher tolerance for uncertainty and failure than traditional business activities . therefore , the metrics should capture both the immediate results and the potential future value of the ventures , as well as the learning and experimentation that they generate . 
 - how to account for the diversity and complexity of the ventures ? corporate venturing can involve a wide range of activities and models , such as internal incubation , external collaboration , corporate venture capital , corporate accelerators , and more . each of these models may have different objectives , processes , and outcomes , and may require different types of metrics and indicators to assess their performance and impact . 
 - how to align the metrics with the stakeholders ' expectations and interests ? corporate venturing involves multiple stakeholders , both internal and external , such as the corporate leadership , the business units , the venture teams , the customers , the partners , the investors , and the society . each of these stakeholders may have different views and criteria for evaluating the success and value of the ventures , and may demand different types of information and evidence . therefore , the metrics should be transparent , consistent , and relevant for the different audiences and purposes . 
 - how to collect and analyze the data and information for the metrics ? corporate venturing often involves dealing with incomplete , ambiguous , or qualitative data and information , as well as dynamic and evolving contexts and environments . therefore , the metrics should be flexible , adaptable , and scalable , and should leverage both quantitative and qualitative methods and sources to capture the richness and diversity of the innovation phenomena . 
 given these challenges , some of the best practices and recommendations for developing and using innovation metrics in corporate venturing are : 
 - define the metrics based on the strategic objectives and vision of the corporate venturing unit , and align them with the overall corporate goals and values . the metrics should reflect the purpose and mission of the corporate venturing unit , and should support the decision - making and communication processes within and outside the organization . the metrics should also be consistent and coherent with the corporate culture and values , and should foster a positive and constructive attitude towards innovation and risk - taking . 
 - use a balanced and comprehensive set of metrics that cover the different dimensions and perspectives of innovation . the metrics should capture the inputs , outputs , outcomes , and impacts of the ventures , as well as the processes and behaviors that enable and drive innovation . the metrics should also consider the different levels and units of analysis , such as the individual , the team , the venture , the portfolio , and the ecosystem . the metrics should also account for the different types and stages of innovation , such as incremental , radical , disruptive , exploratory , exploitative , and more . 
 - use a mix of quantitative and qualitative metrics that complement and enrich each other . the metrics should leverage both hard and soft data and information , such as financial , operational , customer , social , environmental , and more . the metrics should also use both objective and subjective measures , such as indicators , ratings , feedback , stories , and more . the metrics should also employ both descriptive and predictive analytics , such as historical , current , and future data and information . 
 - use a dynamic and adaptive approach to measure and evaluate innovation . the metrics should be updated and revised regularly , based on the feedback and learning from the data and information collected and analyzed . the metrics should also be customized and tailored to the specific characteristics and needs of each venture , model , and context . the metrics should also be tested and validated , to ensure their reliability , validity , and usefulness . 
 some examples of how leading companies have applied these best practices and used innovation metrics in corporate venturing are : 
 - google uses a framework called objectives and key results ( okrs ) to set and track the goals and metrics for its corporate venturing activities , such as google x , google ventures , and google capital . the okrs are defined and aligned at the corporate , unit , and venture levels , and are reviewed and updated quarterly . the okrs include both quantitative and qualitative metrics , such as revenue , growth , user satisfaction , social impact , and more . the okrs also encourage ambitious and aspirational goals , as well as learning and experimentation . 
 - procter & gamble uses a framework called innovation productivity to measure and evaluate the performance and impact of its corporate venturing activities , such as connect + develop , p&g ventures , and p&g growthworks . the innovation productivity framework consists of four metrics : innovation sales , innovation margin , innovation success rate , and innovation speed . these metrics capture the financial and operational results and efficiency of the ventures , as well as the quality and speed of the innovation processes . 
 - ibm uses a framework called innovation value scorecard to measure and evaluate the value and impact of its corporate venturing activities , such as ibm research , ibm ventures , and ibm watson . the innovation value scorecard consists of four metrics : revenue impact , profit impact , market impact , and strategic impact . these metrics capture the direct and indirect contributions and benefits of the ventures , as well as the alignment and differentiation of the innovation strategy .

 4. how to anticipate and adapt to the changing innovation landscape ? 
 adapt to changing 
 the future trends and opportunities in corporate venturing are constantly evolving , requiring organizations to anticipate and adapt to the changing innovation landscape . in this section , we will explore various insights from different perspectives to provide a comprehensive understanding of this topic . 
 1. collaboration and partnerships : one key trend in corporate venturing is the emphasis on collaboration and partnerships . companies are increasingly recognizing the value of working together with startups , universities , and other organizations to foster innovation . by forming strategic alliances , companies can leverage external expertise , access new markets , and accelerate the development of innovative solutions . 
 2. technology integration : another important trend is the integration of technology into corporate venturing strategies . emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence , blockchain , and internet of things ( iot ) are reshaping industries and creating new opportunities for innovation . companies that embrace these technologies and incorporate them into their venturing initiatives are better positioned to stay competitive and drive growth . 
 3. focus on sustainability : with the growing awareness of environmental and social issues , corporate venturing is increasingly aligning with sustainability goals . companies are investing in ventures that address climate change , renewable energy , circular economy , and social impact . by integrating sustainability into their innovation vision , organizations can not only contribute to a better future but also attract customers and investors who prioritize sustainability . 
 4. global expansion : corporate venturing is no longer limited to local markets . companies are expanding their venturing activities globally to tap into new markets and access diverse talent pools . this trend is driven by the increasing interconnectedness of the global economy and the need for companies to stay ahead of emerging trends and technologies in different regions . 
 5. data - driven decision making : in the era of big data , companies are leveraging data analytics and insights to drive their venturing strategies . by analyzing market trends , consumer behavior , and industry dynamics , organizations can make informed decisions about which ventures to pursue and how to allocate resources effectively . data - driven decision making enables companies to mitigate risks and maximize the chances of success in their venturing initiatives . 
 to illustrate these trends , let 's consider an example . company xyz , a leading technology firm , has embraced corporate venturing as part of its innovation strategy . they have formed strategic partnerships with startups in the artificial intelligence space to leverage their expertise and access cutting - edge technologies . additionally , they have expanded their venturing activities to emerging markets in asia , recognizing the growth potential in those regions . by integrating sustainability into their venturing initiatives , company xyz has also invested in ventures focused on renewable energy and environmental conservation . 
 in summary , the future of corporate venturing is shaped by trends such as collaboration , technology integration , sustainability , global expansion , and data - driven decision making . by anticipating and adapting to these trends , organizations can stay ahead of the curve and drive innovation in an ever - changing landscape . 
 how to anticipate and adapt to the changing innovation landscape - corporate venturing strategy : how to define and execute your innovation vision and objectives 
 5. how to create a corporate venturing culture and mindset in your organization ? 
 creating a corporate venturing culture and mindset in your organization is crucial for fostering innovation and driving growth . by embracing a culture of corporate venturing , companies can tap into new opportunities , explore disruptive ideas , and stay ahead in today 's dynamic business landscape . 
 to cultivate a corporate venturing culture , it is important to encourage an entrepreneurial mindset among employees . this involves promoting risk - taking , embracing failure as a learning opportunity , and empowering individuals to think outside the box . by fostering a culture that values innovation and encourages employees to explore new ideas , organizations can create an environment conducive to corporate venturing . 
 here are some insights from different perspectives on how to create a corporate venturing culture and mindset : 
 1. foster a culture of collaboration : encourage cross - functional collaboration and create platforms for employees to share ideas and collaborate on innovative projects . this can help break down silos and promote a culture of collective problem - solving . 
 2. provide resources and support : allocate dedicated resources , such as funding , time , and expertise , to support corporate venturing initiatives . this sends a clear message that the organization is committed to innovation and provides employees with the necessary tools to explore new ideas . 
 3. encourage intrapreneurship : identify and nurture intrapreneurs within the organization – individuals who possess an entrepreneurial spirit and drive for innovation . provide them with opportunities to lead projects , take ownership , and make a meaningful impact . 
 4. embrace open innovation : look beyond the boundaries of the organization and collaborate with external partners , startups , and academia . this can bring fresh perspectives , access to new technologies , and opportunities for co - creation . 
 5. establish clear goals and metrics : define clear objectives for corporate venturing initiatives and establish metrics to measure success . this helps align efforts , track progress , and ensure accountability . 
 6. celebrate and learn from failures : encourage a culture where failures are seen as valuable learning experiences . celebrate efforts , even if they don't always lead to success , and create a safe space for experimentation and risk - taking . 
 7. provide training and development : invest in training programs that enhance employees ' entrepreneurial skills , such as design thinking , agile methodologies , and innovation management . this equips them with the tools and mindset needed to drive corporate venturing initiatives . 
 remember , these are just some insights on creating a corporate venturing culture and mindset . each organization is unique , and it 's important to tailor these approaches to fit your specific context and goals .

# Startups Revolutionizing Carbon Accounting for Corporations  

The global push for decarbonization has spurred innovation in carbon accounting startups, which empower corporations to measure, manage, and reduce emissions effectively. These platforms leverage technology, automation, and data integration to address the complexities of greenhouse gas (GHG) reporting. This report examines leading startups in the space, their business frameworks, and strategies for enabling corporate sustainability.  

---

## Key Startups in Carbon Accounting  

### **1. Carbon Analytics (UK)**  
Carbon Analytics provides an AI-driven SaaS platform for automating GHG emissions tracking and reporting. Founded in 2013, it focuses on simplifying scope 1, 2, and 3 emissions calculations using primary and secondary data sources. Its tools integrate with existing accounting systems, enabling real-time carbon footprint monitoring and compliance with standards like ISO 14064 and the GHG Protocol【2】【3】【4】. The platform emphasizes accessibility for SMEs, reducing reliance on costly consultancy services【2】.  

### **2. Greenly (France)**  
Established in 2019, Greenly offers a cloud-based platform that automates emissions calculations while ensuring alignment with the Science-Based Targets initiative (SBTi) and the GHG Protocol. Its framework includes features for carbon offsetting and stakeholder engagement, positioning it as a leader in execution strength and market reach【1】.  

### **3. Persefoni (Global)**  
Persefoni specializes in audit-grade carbon accounting for mid-to-large enterprises, particularly in legal and professional services. Its AI-powered platform addresses complex scope 3 emissions tracking, ensuring compliance with evolving regulatory requirements【6】. The company’s focus on accuracy and scalability makes it a preferred choice for organizations with multi-location operations【6】.  

### **4. Notch (UK)**  
Notch, launched in 2025, builds on activity-based data to deliver customizable carbon accounting solutions. It leverages a partner model to connect businesses with international collaborators, enabling tailored strategies for decarbonization. The platform adheres to GHG Protocol standards and supports scalability as companies expand their reporting scope【10】.  

### **5. Workiva (US)**  
Workiva’s Carbon solution integrates carbon accounting with financial and ESG reporting. It automates data collection across scopes 1-3, aligns with frameworks like the EU CSRD, and facilitates collaboration with suppliers. The platform’s emphasis on audit-ready documentation positions it as a one-stop solution for compliance-driven enterprises【8】.  

---

## Business Frameworks and Strategies  

### **Technology-Driven Automation**  
Startups like Carbon Analytics and Persefoni utilize AI and machine learning to automate data integration from energy consumption, supply chain, and procurement systems【2】【6】. This reduces manual effort and minimizes errors in emissions calculations.  

### **Compliance and Standardization**  
Adherence to global standards such as the GHG Protocol, ISO 14064, and SBTi is central to these platforms. For example, Carbon Analytics ensures alignment with ISO 14067 for product carbon footprinting, while Workiva’s solution streamlines compliance with SEC climate rules and EU CSRD【3】【8】.  

### **Scalability and Accessibility**  
Startups prioritize scalable SaaS models to serve SMEs and large enterprises. Carbon Analytics simplifies scope 3 reporting for SMEs in complex supply chains【2】, while Notch offers customizable platforms for businesses of all sizes【10】.  

### **Partnership Ecosystems**  
Collaborations with consultants and industry networks enhance credibility. Notch partners with climate consultancy CBN Expert to provide independent advisory services【10】, and Greenly integrates with third-party data sources for comprehensive reporting【1】.  

---

## Challenges and Industry Trends  

### **Data Integration Complexities**  
Scope 3 emissions, which account for 70% of a company’s carbon footprint on average, remain the most challenging to track due to fragmented data sources. Startups like Persefoni and Carbon Analytics use hierarchical data models to automate supply chain emissions【2】【6】.  

### **Regulatory Pressures**  
Increasing regulations, such as the EU CSRD and SEC climate disclosures, drive demand for audit-ready platforms. Workiva’s integration of carbon accounting with financial reporting reflects this trend【8】.  

### **Market Fragmentation**  
The carbon accounting market is highly fragmented, with over 158 startups identified in 2025【7】. This competition necessitates differentiation through specialized features, such as Persefoni’s focus on legal sectors【6】.  

---

## Conclusion  

Startups in carbon accounting are reshaping corporate sustainability by combining automation, compliance, and scalability. While challenges like data integration and regulatory complexity persist, these platforms are critical for enabling businesses to meet net-zero goals. As demand for transparency grows, the industry will likely see further innovation in AI-driven analytics and cross-sector partnerships.  

---

 what is carbon accounting software ? 
 definition 
 carbon accounting software enables companies to collate their carbon data , measure and report their carbon footprint , set scientific targets , and plan to reduce their emissions in one unified platform . 
 leading carbon accounting software is decarbonisation - first : certified calculations power the identification of the reduction actions with the biggest potential .

 the 12 best carbon accounting software

 the platform embeds ai to guide you through data mapping , memorise your conventions and custom systems , and detects anomalies . it also helps you connect the dots from the data to the report , and from the report to the action plan . the tool lets you use decarbonisation scenarios and project return on investment .

 explore plan a ’s software today 
 2. ibm 's environmental intelligence suite 
 ibm 's environmental intelligence suite is a legacy software for data and emissions management designed to assist organisations with data and emissions management . the suite incorporates basic climate risk analytics powered by artificial intelligence , offering tools for risk assessment and response . it aims to integrate carbon accounting functionalities into broader business operations , providing a platform for companies to monitor and manage their environmental impact . 
 the suite also includes features for weather forecasting and geospatial analytics , which can be utilised to assess potential climate - related risks to business operations . while the software provides a range of capabilities , it may not offer the level of customisation that some organisations require for their specific needs . the suite 's interface and user experience are designed to be accessible , though some users might find it less intuitive compared to more modern , specialised carbon accounting tools 
 3. salesforce 's net zero cloud 
 salesforce 's net zero cloud is a carbon accounting and sustainability management platform designed to help enterprises track and reduce their carbon emissions . the solution leverages salesforce 's cloud - based infrastructure to provide data analytics and reporting capabilities . net zero cloud allows companies to measure their carbon footprint across scope 1, 2, and 3 emissions , set science - based targets , and monitor progress towards sustainability goals . 
 the platform offers features such as simplified data collection , dashboards , and integration with other salesforce products . net zero cloud also includes tools for scenario planning and forecasting , enabling organisations to work on different approaches to emissions reduction . additionally , the software provides carbon offset management capabilities and supports working on various sustainability reporting frameworks . 
 4. microsoft sustainability cloud 
 microsoft sustainability cloud offers a suite of tools designed to help organisations document and report their environmental impact . at the core of this solution is the sustainability manager , which enables businesses to collect , analyse , and visualise sustainability data . the platform integrates with existing microsoft systems , potentially streamlining the data collection process for companies already using microsoft products . 
 while microsoft positions the sustainability cloud for mid - market and smb clients , its scalability for larger enterprises or more complex sustainability reporting needs is less clear . the solution provides features for carbon accounting , water consumption tracking , and waste management reporting . however , as with many emerging sustainability software solutions , its effectiveness may vary depending on the specific requirements and data sources of individual organisations 
 5. sphera 
 sphera , a company owned by the blackstone group , offers an esg ( environmental , social , and governance ) and risk management platform . the software aims to centralise emissions reporting and data management , aiming to integrate safety and sustainability management across organisations . sphera 's solution is being developed to help businesses track and report their carbon emissions , as well as manage other environmental and safety - related data . 
 the platform provides tools for collecting and analysing data from various sources within a company 's operations . it offers features such as carbon accounting , life cycle assessment , and regulatory compliance tracking . sphera 's software is utilised by companies across multiple industries , including manufacturing , energy , and chemicals , to support their sustainability initiatives and meet reporting requirements . 
 6. ibm envizi 
 envizi , recently acquired by ibm , is a sustainability and emissions management platform . it aims to enable organisations to capture , track , and manage emissions data across their operations . the software provides tools for collecting and consolidating environmental data from various sources , including energy consumption , waste generation , and transportation emissions . envizi 's analytics and reporting capabilities can assist companies in meeting their compliance obligations and driving sustainable practices . 
 the platform offers some features to support carbon accounting and broader environmental management . these include simplified data collection , dashboards , and the ability to generate reports for various sustainability frameworks and standards . envizi can also communicate with other enterprise systems , allowing for a more integrated approach to sustainability management within an organisation 's existing infrastructure . the software caters to a diverse range of industries , from manufacturing and retail to healthcare and financial services .

 cority 's environmental cloud platform is a comprehensive solution designed to assist organisations in managing their environmental compliance and data across various domains , including air , water , waste , and chemical management . the platform centralises environmental data from multiple sources , providing a unified view of an organisation 's environmental performance . it offers tools for data collection , analysis , and reporting , which can be utilised to track and manage carbon emissions as part of broader sustainability initiatives . 
 in addition to its core environmental management capabilities , cority 's platform includes features for sustainability reporting and greenhouse gas ( ghg ) emissions tracking . the software allows users to calculate their carbon footprint based on collected data and generate reports that align with various international standards and frameworks . while the platform 's primary focus is on environmental compliance , its data management and analytical tools can support organisations in their efforts to monitor and reduce their carbon emissions over time . 
 8. workiva 
 workiva , a company primarily recognised for its esg reporting software , has expanded its offerings to include some carbon tracking capabilities . the workiva carbon solution enables businesses to collect , manage , and report greenhouse gas emissions data across various use cases . this platform can communicate with financial and operational systems , aiming to facilitate data collection and analysis .

 in addition to these features , sinai 's solution includes capabilities for internal carbon pricing and transition risk management . the platform allows users to create dynamic carbon budgets and evaluate various mitigation options . sinai technologies , headquartered in san francisco with an office in são paulo , serves clients across different industries . 
 11. klimahelden 
 klimahelden 's digital climate manager is a software solution designed to assist companies in managing their carbon footprint . the platform provides tools for tracking , analysing , and reducing co2 emissions across various business operations . users can calculate their emissions based on input data and generate reports to gain insights into their environmental impact . 
 the software also offers features for developing emission reduction strategies and communicating sustainability efforts to stakeholders . klimahelden 's solution includes offsetting options , allowing companies to compensate for their unavoidable emissions through certified projects . 
 12. sami 
 sami 's product provides a suite of tools that aims to assist companies in measuring , reducing , and reporting their carbon emissions . the platform features capabilities for carbon accounting , and data collection from various sources . additionally , sami develops tools for reduction planning , allowing businesses to set and track emission reduction targets . 
 to support its users , sami 's platform includes access to sector - specific consultants who can provide tailored guidance . the company also offers training options to help organisations better understand and utilise the software . notably , some businesses may be eligible for certain grants when implementing sami 's solution , potentially offsetting some of the costs associated with adopting carbon accounting practices 
 essential features to look for in carbon accounting software 
 here are 6 critical features businesses should prioritise when searching for a carbon accounting solution : 
 1. intuitive and powerful data collection 
 to ensure accurate and efficient carbon accounting , interfaces for manual input , bulk imports , and api connections help maintain data hygiene and reduce errors . a capable software should also leverage ai 
 2. accurate corporate carbon footprint ( ccf ) calculations 
 automates the calculation of a company 's carbon footprint , enabling precise measurement of ghg emissions across all scopes . this provides the baseline for reporting and target setting . 
 3. detailed carbon emissions reporting 
 facilitates detailed ghg disclosures for regulatory , voluntary , and value chain reporting . supports the generation of reports in various formats , including ready - to - publish pdfs , raw csvs and api for larger businesses . 
 4. strategic decarbonisation target setting 
 assists in setting and visualising emission reduction targets using methodologies like science - based targets ( sbts ) . features intuitive charts and graphs for effective progress tracking . 
 let your platform identify key areas of decarbonisation 
 5. advanced progress tracking and analytics 
 provides continuous monitoring of emissions and the net - zero journey with dashboards and visual insights . advanced analytics empower sustainability teams to make data - driven decisions . 
 powerful customisable dashboards that allow you to create credible scenarios for your stakeholders ( credit : plan a ) 
 6. effective decarbonisation action planning 
 identifies critical areas for emission reduction and integrates scope 3 data for comprehensive decarbonisation plans . it recommends and manages projects through an intuitive interface ; ensuring efficient , value - chain - wide emissions reduction . 
 your decarbonisation plan should be precisely numbered to generate buy - in 
 using a dedicated carbon management software versus building internal solutions 
 internal solutions , often using multiple spreadsheets and scattered data , lack the expertise and accuracy needed for emissions analysis . a sap survey found that only a third of mid - market executives are satisfied with their data quality , and 86 % still use spreadsheets for emissions tracking . 
 switching to carbon accounting software simplifies data collection , automates calculations , and improves accuracy . read our 11 reasons why you should not use spreadsheets for carbon accounting in our dedicated article . 
 as a carbon accounting expert , i strongly advocate using sustainability software over internal solutions . unlike cumbersome internal solutions reliant on spreadsheets , advanced software offers efficient data collection , accurate emissions calculations , streamlined data integration across departments , and enhanced stakeholder transparency . this allows for vast time and cost savings whilst strengthening brand resilience and mitigating risks related to compliance and sustainability commitments . 
 johannes weber , director of sustainability solutions @ plan a. 
 how to choose the best carbon accounting software for your company ? 
 to ensure you choose a solution that aligns with your sustainability goals and operational needs , we recommend asking these 12 questions when evaluating carbon footprint software : 
 question relevance 
 1. does the software prioritise decarbonisation over offsetting ? focusing on decarbonisation ensures long - term emissions reductions , rather than relying heavily on offsets which may not contribute directly to reducing carbon at the source . 
 2. can the software track emissions across all emissions scopes and categories ? full scope 1, 2, and 3 coverage ensures a complete view of your carbon footprint , including both direct and indirect emissions , enabling better reduction strategies . 
 3. is the carbon calculation method certified for compliance with the ghg protocol ( e . g . by tüv rheinland ) ? certification guarantees that the software follows recognised standards , ensuring accuracy and credibility in your carbon reporting . 
 4. does the platform provide comprehensive data analysis tools ( e . g . custom dashboards ) ? robust analysis and visualisation tools help track performance , identify trends , and support informed decisions to meet your sustainability goals . 
 5. does the platform provide an api to integrate with your existing tools ? seamless integration reduces manual data entry , improves accuracy , and ensures that emissions data is regularly updated across all systems . 
 6. does it recommend reduction actions based on your company ’s emission profile ? custom reduction recommendations help focus efforts on the most impactful areas , maximising your emissions reduction potential . 
 7. does the software provide additional support for esg reporting , such as a csrd module ? built - in esg reporting features ensure compliance with regulatory requirements and make reporting more efficient and transparent . 
 8. does the provider share educational content through expert sessions and in - platform insights ? ongoing learning and insights inform your team about best practices , helping you optimise software usage and stay updated on industry trends . 
 9. is the platform ’s interface user - friendly and intuitive ? a simple , intuitive interface encourages user adoption and ensures that teams can work efficiently without extensive training . 
 10. is personalised expert support available to help with your company ’s specific requirements ? tailored expert support helps address specific challenges , ensuring the software meets your unique sustainability needs . 
 11. is the software provider well - established in the industry and backed by customer references ? a proven track record and strong customer references demonstrate reliability and successful implementation across other businesses . 
 12. is the provider committed to its own sustainability practices , such as b - corp certification ? providers with strong sustainability commitments ensure alignment with your values and enhance the credibility of your efforts . 
 companies looking to make a meaningful impact on the environment must choose a carbon accounting software aligned with ghg protocol methodology . ghg protocol supplies the world 's most widely used greenhouse gas accounting and is essential for ensuring accuracy and reliable carbon management . from an operational perspective - prioritising a platform that is easy to use , provides intuitive and data - driven insights , and has a team of real - world climate experts behind it is essential to setting your organisation up for sustainability success .

 20 frameworks , startup intelligence & more !

 our innovation analysts recently looked into emerging technologies and up - and - coming startups working on innovative solutions to mitigate carbon emissions . as there is a large number of startups working on a wide variety of solutions , we decided to share our insights with you . this time , we are taking a look at 5 promising carbon accounting startups . 
 heat map : 5 top carbon accounting startups 
 using our star tus insights discovery platform , covering 1 . 379 . 000 + startups & scaleups globally , we looked at innovation in the field of carbon emissions management . for this research , we identified 158 relevant solutions and picked 5 to showcase below . these companies were chosen based on a data - driven startup scouting approach , taking into account factors such as location , founding year , and relevance of technology , among others . depending on your specific criteria , the top picks might look entirely different . 
 the global startup heat map below highlights 5 startups & scaleups developing carbon accounting and offsetting solutions . moreover , the heat map reveals regions that observe a high startup activity and illustrates the geographic distribution of all 158 companies we analyzed for this specific topic .

 cloverly – carbon offsetting for businesses 
 all business activities , whether it is a product or a service , directly or indirectly produce carbon emissions . digital services utilize energy - intensive servers , emissions from the manufacturing of any product , as well as services that utilize some form of energy . moreover , there is a consensus that humans cannot achieve absolute zero - emissions . this drives emerging environment - focused startups to provide solutions for businesses to at least achieve carbon neutrality . 
 cloverly is a us - based startup that offers a sustainability - as - a - service platform to offset carbon emissions for businesses . the startup ’s application programming interface ( api ) calculates emissions and matches it , in real - time , with suitable carbon offset projects . for example , the cloverly api calculates emissions from flights or vehicle fleets to offset the impact of the activity . 
 veridium lab – natural capital markets 
 environmental assets are playing an increasingly larger role in capital markets . international agreements , such as the paris climate agreement , highlight the role of natural capital markets in fighting global warming . startups and scaleups are developing novel market mechanisms that are transparent and based on standardized carbon accounting rules . 
 hong kong - based startup veridium labsis creating a blockchain - based tokenized marketplace for carbon trading . the startup ’ seco smart protocol enables companies to offset the environmental impact of their activities in a transparent manner . the solution also allows carbon - emitting companies to account for the cost of offsetting in their products and services . 
 tomorrow – electricity carbon footprint measurement 
 many businesses today are still unaware of their carbon footprint , and hence , make no effort to offset their emissions . a lack of understanding about carbon trading , and some key challenges in evaluating the impact of such schemes , encourage startups to find alternative solutions . global data collection across industries , along with granular segments within them , also provide a base for tailoring and implementing carbon - reduction solutions . 
 danish startup tomorrow is building electricity map , an api platform to measure the carbon footprint of electricity consumption . electricity map provides access to data relating to carbon intensity and power breakdowns from more than 200 countries . cloud computing , electric vehicle charging , and heating or cooling are some applications of the startup ’s api to manage carbon dioxide ( co 2 ) emissions . 
 clair ifi – oil & gas carbon emission management 
 globally , national and subnational government organizations are drawing up strict regulations and requirements for polluting entities . for large polluting industries such as oil & gas , meeting new environmental standards poses a significant challenge . moreover , with numerous polluting outlets from a single site , startups are applying artificial intelligence ( ai ) techniques to improve regulatory compliance . 
 canadian startup clair ifi provides a cloud - based interactive platform to facilitate communication among internal teams , industry experts , and regulatory reporting systems for the oil & gas sector . the platform offers real - time insights and projections by quantifying monthly fuel , flare , vent , and emission rates . further , the platform automatically creates compliance reports for multiple regulatory requirements . these include compliance relating to greenhouse gases ( ghg ) , national pollutant release inventory ( npri ) , multi - sector air pollutant regulations ( msapr ) , and methane reduction requirements . 
 carbon grid protocol – carbon offsetting for blockchain networks 
 increasingly , blockchain technology is being used in numerous industries from finance , logistics , healthcare , and energy . however , blockchain transactions currently utilize significant amounts of energy , resulting in high amounts of carbon emissions . this encourages startups and scaleups to develop solutions to offset emissions arising from employing blockchain technology . 
 carbon grid is a singapore - based startup aiming to decarbonize blockchain technology . the start up ’ scarbon grid protocol , c grid , creates an economic framework to reward blockchain networks and decentralized applications ( dapps ) for offsetting their carbon footprint . c grid creates a complementary protocol layer that provides economic incentives to blockchain developers to access carbon credits and maintain carbon neutrality .

8.title: Meet Workiva Carbon: See Audit-Ready Carbon Accounting in Action | Workiva
8.content:
webinar on demand 
 meet workiva carbon : see audit - ready carbon accounting in action 
 in this video 
 workiva hosts a launch webinar introducing their new workiva carbon solution , a comprehensive carbon management platform for emissions disclosure and decarbonization . the presentation covers the market landscape of increasing carbon disclosure regulations including sec climate rules , california sb 253 , and eu csrd , driving companies toward compliance - focused decarbonization strategies . the team demonstrates the platform 's four pillars : measure ( greenhouse gas calculators across scopes 1-3 with automated data integrations ) , manage ( science - based target setting and decarbonization project tracking ) , collaborate ( supplier engagement and data sharing ) , and report ( automated alignment with esg disclosure frameworks ) . key features include ai - powered emissions factor selection , thousands of pre - built utility and erp integrations , supplier database with publicly available emissions data , audit - ready documentation , and seamless integration with workiva 's existing esg and financial reporting platforms . the solution serves both regulated companies meeting disclosure requirements and their suppliers needing to provide emissions data , positioning workiva as the only integrated platform combining carbon accounting with financial and esg reporting . 
 video transcript 
 good morning , good afternoon , everyone . thank you so much for joining us for this super exciting day where we 're going to give you a first look at workiva carbon . so many of you are here because you saw the exciting news that we have officially launched a carbon management solution for our customers and for the market . we are having a packed agenda today . 
 we only have thirty minutes with you all , so we are going to dive in as quickly as possible and allow for as much time as questions questions as we can throughout the duration of our time together . so first things first , a few things on housekeeping items . you will receive a recording to this webinar , so many of you have dialed in from the united states , but we significant portion of folks from europe , and asia pacific who registered . 
 we recognize it 's a little late for you all , so you will be receiving the recording questions . please do submit those through the q and a portion of your on24 platform . we have a team of us on the backside who will try to get to as many of those questions as possible , and if we get to the end and have an opportunity , we will answer some of those live for the audience . 
 other than that , are the two most important things to know is ask questions . we 're here to answer them . and if we can't get to them , we will follow - up with you . we expect that you have a lot of questions . we have many answers and we still have some questions as well as the newness of this kind of sinks in for the workiva organization . so with me today i have alyssa and jasmine and i cannot be more thrilled to have their expertise on the team . 
 my name is mackenzie keller and martin , rather . that was my previous last name , but mackenzie martin . i am a director of product marketing . and what that means is i spend a lot of time with our customers . i spend a lot of time with our partners trying to determine what are the solutions that our customers need to do their jobs more efficiently . and with that , we saw that carbon management , decarbonization and carbon accounting was a massive part of the work that our sustainability professionals were doing . 
 and we wanted to solve for that . and we identified through having countless conversations with our customers and with the market . this was the time for us to transition and to launch workiva carbon . so what we 'll do today is talk high level about the different capabilities and features that are embedded in the solution . the best part is this works and integrates with your existing esg solution platform and your other workiva solutions . 
 we 'll talk a little bit more about what that connectivity looks like during webinar . so i 'm going to turn it over to alyssa . alyssa is the previous chief sustainability officer at sustain life . she 's transitioned officially this week over to the workiva carbon team , and we could not be more thrilled to have her and her expertise . she 's going to walk us through the solution , the value that you will see for your customers if you 're a partner on the line , and also the value that you'll see if you will be the user on the inside . 
 so alyssa , i will turn it over to you . thanks so much , mac . it is an honor and a pleasure to be here . the first webinar of many , i am sure . and thanks to all those on the line who are taking a little bit of time out of their day , to spend it with workiva carbon . so i want to start with just a little bit of a high level landscape and a little bit of market trends of what 's been going on in the emissions disclosure and kind of carbon space . 
 so the market has evolved to a kind of perfect , in my opinion , nexus of voluntary decarbonization targets and corporate strategy intersecting with a global suite of disclosure regulations . and so while we 're often talking about this alphabet soup of esg and the efforts to harmonize across the seemingly endless acronyms that comprise that soup , there 's actually an incredible harmonization that 's going on right now that 's really anchoring on emissions disclosure . 
 that 's really the common thread throughout all of these voluntary frameworks , the mandated disclosures , they all include carbon disclosure . and so while net zero planning kind of began as a relatively modest or niche group of companies that were real leaders in their industry , it 's become really a lot more commonplace as an indication of long term planning and resilience . 
 and i think where the market is today is that it has come to really expect emissions disclosure as an indication of risk planning and value creation and responsible forward thinking business strategy . it 's kind of an indication of all of that . and so today almost half of the forbes global two thousand have already set emission reduction targets . so we really see this spreading in how kind widespread and common it is . 
 and then of course you have all of these regulations that are coming into force . so the voluntary frameworks that kind of guide companies and have traditionally guided companies to establish their net zero targets , they 're really acting as a guide for these regulations that are now coming on board across widespread global jurisdictions . and what these regulations are doing is really formalizing the ways in which companies have to disclose this information . 
 because up until now , despite having these frameworks , these voluntary frameworks , the disclosure has been somewhat inconsistent . and so it makes comparison of that information that the stakeholders are requesting a little bit more challenging . and so these regulations are coming in force , they 're coming in fast and they 're coming at incredible scale . 
 if we just walk through a couple of the highlights this past march , the sec finally approved its climate disclosure rule and that 's going to require all publicly traded companies and foreign registrants to disclose climate related information , including emissions in their annual , registered , regulated financial filings . then in twenty twenty three , california couldn't quite wait for that sec rule to pass . 
 so it adopted an even more ambitious rule sb two fifty three , which is requiring any company regardless of public private ownership to disclose emissions across scopes one , two and three . we of course have csrd in the eu , which is the most robust and ambitious sustainability disclosure law . and we have the first round of companies that need to report to that for twenty twenty four data , so activities that are happening now , in twenty twenty five . 
 and so that requires not only the disclosure of emissions , but also to actually establish transition plans and decarbonization towards a net zero economy . so that 's really the most ambitious of these laws . and then you have a whole host of jurisdictions like new zealand and singapore , hong kong , japan that have all adopted similar emissions disclosure laws for their primary listed exchange companies . 
 so we basically have this market dynamic now where companies are increasingly approaching their decarbonization strategy and adjacent reporting through a lens of compliance . and that 's what 's new about this because the stakes are kind of higher now . the investors and the capital markets have quite frankly demanded this information , that voluntary disclosure was happening because investors were requesting requesting it of their companies . 
 and so they determined that this is a material to their investment decisions and they 're demanding that regulators put in place consistent and enforceable requirements so that they can compare across somewhat of comparable baseline and benchmark . at the very same time that the regulated companies are driving towards this compliance , market leaders are still focusing on that scope three supply chain . 
 so you've got a lot of big names , companies like walmart and amazon and microsoft that are continuing to set the bar higher and set that new standard for supplier engagement and performance . so that 's doing things like requiring emissions reporting on an annual basis , including requirements and rfps . so if suppliers want to win that business , they 're required now to figure out a way to measure their emissions in a reputable , regular and automated , effective , efficient manner . 
 so i like to think of this high level as like this triple play dynamic where you have industry leaders that are continuing to push that bar higher , regulation coming in to kind of standardize and raise the floor of the requirements and then suppliers that again aren't directly mandated themselves by these rules but are still compelled by business imperative of maintaining their customer base are now deepening their own progress to meet demands . 
 so let 's talk a little bit about our strategy here . that dynamic that i just explained , that 's what we've launched workiva carbon in to really address . and the key here is all about balancing powerful technology with an easy to use platform . so this is work that historically has been done a lot of the time in spreadsheets , whether it was done in house by a company or with supportive consultants and oftentimes through a somewhat black box of a software platform that lacked transparency . 
 so on the excel side , there 's a lot of manual errors not to mention the administrative overhead of updating emission factors and data sources and all the kind of nuance that goes into carbon accounting , which again has become a lot more rigorous in a very short period of time . so we have technology as the clear solution because it is after all mostly an accounting exercise . 
 and so just as financial accounting digitized to tools and softwares , so now we 're seeing this for carbon accounting . and so our tools at workiva carbon , they 're intuitive . they empower businesses at varying levels of expertise to meet these requirements . and so that means things like very clear system guidance , built in resources and educational context so that you understand the options and the impact of the different methodologies or ways you may move forward in your accounting exercise . 
 because carbon accounting , i won't say unlike financial accounting , but it is tricky . there are actually different methodologies that can be employed depending on the data available and the nuances of your business . and so to that end , it also means having a platform that is flexible and customizable . and critical to this is also leveraging ai to unlock new efficiencies and innovation in decarbonization . 
 so that is things like emission factor recommendations and selection , vendor mapping for scope three calculations , industry insights and peer comparison , things that have traditionally taken so much time all automated in a digitized suite of tools that are so powerful in providing those key insights . and then of course we can't forget our partner ecosystem of incredible experts to further deepen support of decarbonization and climate strategy alongside the carbon accounting deployed through our tool . 
 okay , so what can we expect from workiva carbon , right ? what 's in it ? we like to orient on pillars of measure , manage , collaborate and report . measure is the core of carbon counting . so this is a suite of greenhouse gas calculators across scopes one hundred twenty three that are leveraging thousands of system integrations to automate utility and erp system data flows . 
 right on the managed side , this is kind of your next step after you've measured your baseline and really gotten your arms around that data . this is where you 're setting your science based targets . you 're assessing esg risk in your supply chain , visualizing different mitigation pathways , engaging suppliers , and really managing and tracking those core decarbonization efforts across your enterprise . 
 and then collaborate . and this is a really important one . and for those that are already engaged kind of in their decarbonization journey and with existing carbon management efforts , you know how critical it is to share , leverage and link trusted and auditable data and deliverables across business functions . and that means internally across our own organization , but externally both with getting information from suppliers as well as sharing information with transparency out to third party auditors . 
 and then of course we can't forget about report , right ? this is the last mile of reporting that 's really driving so much of this , keeping all of the companies accountable to this very exercise . so we are automatically aligning our emissions data to reports that are created within the workiva platform that are , as you know , always audit ready thanks to rigorous data governance tools . 
 so just a little bit now on who we serve . if we didn't make it clear already , we 're catering to companies of all sizes , industries , and maturity because there is a broad spectrum of those . but they 're all unified in their commitment to meet these new compliance requirements and drive towards decarbonization . so that means on one side , the regulated companies that are really feeling this pressure to meet disclosure requirements with a host of new mandates that are really focused on quality control , strong data governance and internal controls . 
 we know how important that is to you , right ? so much of the workiva platform is focused on that . and so extending that same rigor and process to carbon accounting is what you can expect . and then on the other side , of course , the suppliers to those companies that are perhaps maybe a little earlier in their journey , directly mandated themselves , but at the same time still need an automatic embedded system to furnish this information to their requesting buyers with regularity and with confidence . 
 so that 's just a little bit of high level framing . we 'd like to say that there 's no real better way to show you what we 're keeping carbon is all about than just to dive in . so i 'm going to pass it off to jasmine for a whirlwind tour of a product demo . great , thank you , alyssa . so i 'll go ahead and share my screen . but hi everyone , i 'm jasmine zhang , i 'm the director of product management at workiva carbon . 
 and today , i 'm excited to introduce you to the platform and show you what it 's all about . it 's an easy to use solution for streamlining the full life cycle of carbon accounting , carbon management , and decarbonization . and best of all , it 's integrated into that same workiva platform you trust for all of your financial and nonfinancial reporting . so let 's just dive into it . 
 as liz mentioned , the platform centered around the four pillars of the sustainability journey , measure , manage , collaborate , and report . under measure , you can build your complete audit ready emissions inventories across scopes one , two , and three , along with the categories of the greenhouse gas protocol . and you can also track environmental data such as energy consumption from your buildings and vehicles . 
 we have waste production and diversion and water usage . you can track your high level scope categories here as well as your impact by category . in terms of getting data into the platform , we offer multiple data collection methods . so first we really want to emphasize automation through apis , integrations and supplier surveys to save you time on the aspects of getting data into the platform . 
 to do that , our platform has thousands of pre built integrations . here i 'm showing the integrations we have with utility providers globally , and we also have integrations with the most common accounting systems like quickbooks and oracle netsuite to power your purchases data . you can also create custom integrations as needed . and once you set up that integration , your data entries will be created automatically containing the audit trail of all of your attached documents like utility bills . 
 so it 's really set up and be able to get all of your data in seamlessly . in terms of getting data into the platform otherwise , you can also add data manually via form or you can upload in bulk via something like excel . so you can go ahead and do that here with templates or you can also upload raw unstructured data that you can then map to the fields that we need in our system to power all of your carbon calculations . 
 so for example , under buildings , can track your scope one and two emissions . that includes electricity and fuel consumption like natural gas , and we calculate the associated location and market based emissions for scope two . so to calculate emissions for each category , our proprietary ai technology automatically chooses the best matching emissions factor from a library of thousands of third party validated factors . 
 so for these examples , i 'll type in my total kilowatt hour of electricity consumption , my total natural gas . i can also use custom fuel factors that i 've entered into the system , as well as custom overrides . so our system is highly flexible , allowing you to enter both those standard inputs as well as your custom inputs of your own . here you'll see you can also optionally enter associated spend , and that helps you track your budget against activities that are contributing to emissions . 
 we have a flexible grouping feature that allows you to set up a location hierarchy that matches your structure . so here you have your multiple regions listed out and your locations can fit within each of those . you can also set up different entry groups such as business units , and that reflects how you'll want to cut your data downstream . you'll be able to filter your data as well as segment out your data in a way that makes sense to your business . 
 you can set up multiple levels of these multiple types of groups and associate them with your data entries . the location groups will be associated with your locations automatically as you can see here . so each of your tagged entries will already appear in the associated region . so to calculate emissions for each category , in addition to buildings , we also handle a range of inputs to really meet the customer where they are . 
 so for example , under vehicles , you can enter a variety of different inputs . so if you have total fuel usage , that 's really the most accurate and we would prefer you enter that . but if you only have total distance for your fleet or total spend , you can enter that as well and we 'll convert that into total estimated fuel usage before applying emissions factors . 
 so we really understand that customers have a variety of different data inputs and we want to handle and meet customers where they are . i 'll now go into some of our scope three calculators . so i 'll go into our purchases calculator which covers scope three category one and two , so purchased goods and services and capital goods . this calculator streamlines the process of calculating emissions from your purchases data , whether from your accounting platforms or your erp platforms that can be directly integrated into the system so that you can really focus your decarbonization efforts on your top emitting suppliers with the highest mitigation potential . 
 so we 're not all just about reporting and calculating a number , we really want to help guide you onto the next steps of engaging directly with your supply chain . so here we automatically incorporate primary supplier specific data from publicly available data sources . so for example , if your suppliers have already reported their emissions publicly to a source like cdp , we have formed a supplier database where you can leverage that primary data directly on emissions and targets . 
 and you can also collect data directly from your suppliers via the platform via surveys , though we really want to automate as much as possible through our supplier database . so here there 's a few things that you can do to help us calculate the proper emissions and get to as actionable and accurate a scope three inventory as possible . so here , you will map all the suppliers from your purchases data into our emissions database and the suppliers that are available there . 
 we leverage ai models and nlp to guess best matches for your suppliers , and you can always confirm or clear the match or select from our list of available suppliers . once that 's done , you'll be able to save and apply those mappings going forward . and then you can also map your commodities data as well . so these are your internal accounting categories . 
 you can map those over to standard commodities platform and this is to fill the gaps . so anywhere you don't have primary supplier specific data , which is really the cleanest and most accurate data you can have , we can still fill the gaps with spend based estimates that are based on an average emissions factor for the commodity that you've mapped your data to . 
 so here you'll be able to give us those mappings . again , i 've already confirmed some of the suggestions and you can see where we've automated some auto suggestions here . and then once you 're done , you can go ahead and save , apply any additional overrides or add any additional information and then go back to your emissions ledger to view the final results . 
 here you'll be able to see your total spend , total emissions , and emissions intensity , and click in for more details by supplier or commodity . so what next then ? now you've calculated your data , you need to take some next steps . so you can now begin a targeted process of seeing who your top suppliers are , looking at our recommended actions , whether it 's engaging them for more data , reducing use with them or engaging them for reduction . 
 and you can use our platform to actually send a data request to them directly . that way you can get primary supplier specific data in the absence of publicly available data and improve the accuracy of your footprint . that takes me over to our supplier engagement module . so we really understand the value of engaging deeply with your supply chain , not only to better understand your total emissions , but also to work with them to upscale . 
 so they can use our platform to calculate their emissions , set targets , as well as take operational changes to reduce . and that 's really the only way that your scope three emissions can be decreased over time . so here you'll see all the suppliers you've managed through the platform . you have the ability to send a data request to them via the platform and then get that request back from them . 
 so in this example , for my supplier dell , i can see some trends around total emissions and spend with them as well as targets . and then i can also view data they 've reported directly back to me so we can utilize supplier assessments and surveys through our platform to get you more information . so that wraps up the calculation part of our , demo , but i 'll move on to the next steps . 
 so once you've input your activity data , you can use our data reviewer feature to save you time and effort on manual analysis and cleanup . that traditionally takes a lot of effort , but we automatically flag data gaps , duplicates , and anomalies to you for your full footprint so you can then fix those issues yourself . or if you don't have exact data , you can use our estimation tools to help you fill those gaps . 
 and this improves the overall quality of your inventories and supports readiness for taking the next steps , whether that 's setting a science based reduction target or preparing for third party verification and assurance . now on audit and assurance , workiva carbon also ensures that your data is transparent , reliable and ready for those internal or third party audits . 
 so this module provides full transparency into our carbon accounting formulas and factors , and we also provide workflow tools that reduce the need for multiple cycles of back and forth with your auditors . so if i click into one of these data rows , you'll see we are super transparent with the type of information we provide back to our users and their auditors . 
 we provide emission factor sources , values , conversions , formulas , methodologies , and we also add any user attached documents and notes directly here . invited auditors can then sample rows , mark rows as verified or flagged for a view , so needing more comment back from the customer , and collaborating using these flags and notes to streamline communication with their client . 
 on the reporting side , once you've gotten your data checked , and audited , as you input data , you can glean insights and pull data for internal or external review from our analytical dashboards . we have a summary dashboard as well as one built out for every single category . but you can use this visualization to see data in the ways that make sense to your business and identify emissions hotspots and areas for improvement , whether that 's by category or by location . 
 so what next after you enter your data ? under manage , you can set spti aligned targets for scopes one , two , and three emissions in the near or long term . so we help you set targets that meet the criteria of the science based targets initiatives , un recommendations , and iso guidance . and then as you pursue decarbonization initiatives , you can track your progress here , and you'll see whether you 're on or off track to meet your target trajectory . 
 speaking of decarbonization projects , so once you've measured your baseline and set a target , what next ? our platform doesn't just stop there , we help you decarbonize . so under manage , you'll be able to browse our library of hundreds of decarbonization projects with data backed recommendations based on your emissions , hotspots , and your sector . so to help you meet your goals , we actually provide actionable strategies here where you can engage in major initiatives like transitioning to green energy or taking smaller steps like minimizing air travel . 
 so we walk you through step by step what 's recommended here to actually decarbonize . and then lastly , under report , we harmonize your reporting efforts by aligning your data inputs with key esg disclosures across voluntary and mandated frameworks . so here we enable you to create esg reports in alignment with gri , ifrs and tcfd standards , disclose the cdp and conform to regulations like csrd , sb two fifty three and the sec climate rule . 
 so we've already taken everything you've entered into the measure and manage parts of our platform and spit it out directly into the format that you need . and ultimately , this is all integrated back into workiva 's esg reporting platform as well . so you really see the combined power of both our carbon accounting platform and the esg reporting suite . 
 so i 'll just say a few closing words here about the product . so ultimately , our customers save a lot of time and effort on data collection and reporting through all of our automated flows , our powerful calculation engine so you can focus on what 's important , reducing impact through setting targets , engaging with your supply chain , and implementing these decarbonization initiatives . 
 and workiva carbon is now part of the workiva unified platform for assured integrated reporting , so it allows you a really seamless experience of getting your carbon emissions data into our existing trusted platforms . we are now the world 's only integrated saas platform for carbon accounting , decarbonization management , esg , and financial reporting and assurance . 
 so we hope that was really informative , and we 're excited to hear , what you think . with that , i will hand it back to mac to wrap up . thank you so much , jasmine . i think that was the most comprehensive yet speedy demo of a carbon solution i 've ever seen . you guys have inundated us with questions . i think this just goes to show workiva made the absolute right choice by launching to the market to meet the needs of you all . 
 this is super exciting time for us , and i can see the sheer number of our partners , part of our workiva partner network that are on the call today . you guys are just excited , as excited about this opportunity as the customers are , and we could not be more thrilled . with that , we know that you guys have additional questions that we may not have been able to answer on the backside of this webinar . 
 we will continue to answer those . so the webinar itself will conclude in just a moment and i 'll allow jasmine and alyssa maybe to pick one question , to answer before we wrap . if you are a partner on the call today , we've seen a lot of you and have questions . please do reach out to your alliance director . they will have the most information for you . 
 if you are a customer or a prospective customer of workiva carbon , we are working tirelessly around the clock . i kid you not the amount of time , hours and attention that this team has put . we are working for additional engagement opportunities so that you can see a deeper dive into the solution . you can see on our next webinar that we 'll share information on what this connected story looks like with the other solutions that jasmine mentioned that are within the workiva suite . 
 so alyssa , jasmine , is there any other question ? there 's obviously quite a few questions in the box , but is there one maybe you want to ask that has come up frequently from the audience ? i 'll take one . we 're getting a lot of questions around emission factors and the process of monitoring factors for updates . so we maintain a quarterly update process , which means that every single quarter we go through our full suite of emission factor databases to check if there 's been any update to those so we can update the factors automatically in the platform and automate a recalculation for the best factor . 
 that 's something we 're really proud of . we know that it 's market leading . and so that 's getting a lot of questions on that , and how up to date the factors are . yeah , that 's awesome . and that 's perfect for us to know so we can perhaps put a white paper or , a more comprehensive email together to get all of that information in your hands . jasmine , have you had a second to breathe and come off the demo high to look at the q and a ? 
 yes , i see a lot of different questions that are quite detailed . so it seems like everyone has a really good handle on admissions already . but i think i 'll need some more time to just go through and see , what questions make sense to answer . catching up on all of no worries at all . so this brings us to the conclusion of the webinar . we are so excited , for you all to continue to engage with us to learn more . 
 what you'll see on the screen now and what you'll see when you close out on your browser is if you 're interested in having a further conversation with our workiva team about what your current processes are and what your future ambitions are , please do say yes , raise your hand so that we can appropriately prioritize having conversations with you . we will continue to provide webinars , blogs . 
 we will continue to send email updates as we continue to evolve the solution and continue to develop it to your needs . so please do say yes if you want to have a future conversation with us . and again , if you are a partner , please do reach out to your alliance director . they will be the best place for you to get all of your questions answered . so with that , that was probably the most fast and furious webinar of workiva all time . 
 we 're coming back . this isn't the last . this is simply the first of what workiva carbon has to offer . so thank you guys so much for spending your afternoon , your morning with us , and we will see you next time . thanks so much .

analise de carbono para startups
